# Website redesign: status

Last updated: 2026-10-29 (WS01, step 32: a11y sweep; step 31: heritage layout; step 30: heritage fonts; step 29: hero images; step 28: brand marks; step 27: chess data; step 26: status tags; step 25: gold text; step 24: colours; step 23: grounds; step 22: ThemeScope; step 21: dark mode; step 20 opened checkpoint D; checkpoint C, after step 16, step 17 and step 18, is merged; checkpoint D is merged; WS02, step 3: page frame, browser bar colour and rings; step 2: navigation model and signed-in visitor; step 1: record and brief 1.4)

The brief is `docs/redesign/REDESIGN_SPEC.md`. This file records, for each workstream, where it stands, what was decided, where the work differs from the brief, what is left to do, and every `verify:` item that has been checked. It is updated in every redesign PR.

## Ordering rules

1. **The branch is pushed only after the preview database slice is committed.** Every pushed branch gets a Cloudflare Pages preview. Before `[env.preview]` existed in `wrangler.toml`, that preview was bound to the production database `lca-db`, so anyone clicking around it would have written real registrations and accounts. `redesign/ws01-design-system` stays local until the commit that adds the preview database. Before that first push, K also checks the Preview environment's secrets in the Pages dashboard and removes any live Stripe or Resend key: previews existed before this slice and may already hold the live ones.
2. **K migrates the preview database from the branch before reviewing each checkpoint's preview.** He runs `npm run db:migrate:preview` from the branch, with his own Cloudflare credentials, before he looks at the preview, not after the merge. Merging to `main` migrates production only (`.github/workflows/migrate-db.yml`); nothing migrates `lca-db-preview` automatically. Once the branch adds tables the code reads (the sections and schedules tables), a preview bound to an unmigrated database shows errors.
3. **No other branch touches `functions/utils` while checkpoint C is open.** Steps 16 to 19 move files; step 16 moved twenty server helpers into area folders under `functions/utils`. A change to `functions/utils` made on another branch in the meantime would conflict on every moved file, and an import it adds by an old path would break the build after the merge. Step 17 moved nine site library files from `src/lib` into `src/areas`, and the same holds for them: an import another branch adds by an old `src/lib` path breaks the build after the merge. Step 19 moves the domain components the same way: `src/components/tournaments`, `family`, `admin`, `governance`, `maps` and `uscf`, and the two top-level files `src/components/AdminAnnouncementPanel.tsx` and `src/components/RegistrationReminderButton.tsx`, now sit under `src/areas/<area>/components`. A component import another branch adds by one of those old paths breaks the build after the merge too. Until checkpoint C merges, changes to server helpers, the site library and those component folders and files wait or go on `redesign/ws01-design-system`.

## WS01: Design system, themes and accessibility foundation

**Status:** built. All 32 steps are on the branch, built one small step at a time and merged in four checkpoints (A: steps 1 to 8, B: 9 to 15, C: 16 to 19, D: 20 to 32). All four checkpoints are merged into `main` and live, with every switch off; checkpoint D merged on Thursday, October 22, 2026, after a merge-safety review by someone who has not followed the work (see Checkpoint D, after the step 32 block). What WS01 leaves to later workstreams is under Follow-ups.
**Branch:** `redesign/ws01-design-system`, pushed once the preview database step was committed (ordering rule 1), with every step since pushed to it; the head that merged is `ffee346`, the last commit of checkpoint D.
**PR:** checkpoint A was pull request 105, B was 104 and C was 107; checkpoint D (steps 20 to 32) was draft pull request 108, marked ready and merged into `main` as `34b721c` on Thursday, October 22, 2026, so all four are merged.

### What each acceptance criterion and decision is proved by

AC1 to AC14 are the brief's WS01 acceptance criteria. K1a to K6 are the parts of K's October 8 structural decisions. T1 is a step of the plan that neither names: moving the existing pages onto the tokens so they follow dark mode and the looks. T2 is its second half. Each item is proved in one step. "Planned" means that step has not been built yet; the entry is replaced with the passing test, or the recorded measurement, when it lands. Step 32 checks that every row ends with a passing test or a recorded result.

### Step 3: shared `domain/` folder and formats

- New folder `domain/` at the repo root for pure code that the site, the server functions and the workers all use: no database access, no DOM, no Workers types and no React. This step creates `domain/format` only; the other areas (events, registration, households, membership, clubs, live, contracts) are created by the steps that fill them.
- `domain/format` holds `formatScore` (3.5 is "3½", 0.5 is "½", 0 is "0", 10 is "10"), `formatDate` ("Sat, Oct 24", or "Sat, Oct 24, 2026" with the year option), `formatTime` ("7:00 PM", with "12:00 PM" at noon and "12:00 AM" at midnight) and `formatTimeControl` ("G/90+30" becomes "G/90+30 · 90 min each + 30 sec per move"; "G/30;d5" adds "30 min each + 5 sec delay"; "G/60" adds "60 min each"; text it does not recognise comes back unchanged). `describeTimeControl` gives the plain words on their own.
- How values are read: a bare stored date or datetime-local value ("2026-10-24", "2026-10-24T19:00") is Louisiana wall-clock time and is shown as written; a Date, epoch milliseconds or an ISO string with a zone is an instant and is shown in Central time. Columns filled by SQLite's `datetime('now')` (`created_at`, `updated_at`, `sent_at`, `recorded_at` and the like) look like wall-clock text ("2026-10-24 02:30:00") but hold UTC, as the admin audit log, board seats and board inbox already assume by appending `Z`; `formatDate` and `formatTime` read them as UTC when passed `{ stored: 'utc' }` (that example is "Fri, Oct 23" at "9:30 PM"), and the `date.ts` header says those columns must be passed that way. The default stays wall-clock because announcement start and end times are stored as Louisiana time in the same text form. Weekday and month names, and the "7:00 PM" text, are built from fixed tables rather than by `Intl`, so the text is identical in browsers, Node and Workers (newer locale data puts a narrow no-break space before "PM"). A string a helper cannot read is returned as given, so a bad value shows up rather than vanishing.
- `src/lib/format.ts` is one line, `export * from '@domain/format'`, so the brief's path works. Nothing in the site uses the helpers yet, so nothing visible changes and no switch is needed; pages adopt them behind `newLook` in later steps.
- Wiring: `tsconfig.app.json` gains the `@domain/*` path and includes `domain`; `vite.config.ts` and `vitest.config.ts` gain the matching `@domain` alias; `tsconfig.functions.json` now includes `functions`, `domain` and `workers/daily-emails/src`; `workers/daily-emails/tsconfig.json` includes `../../domain`. The server functions and the workers import `domain/` by relative path, as the worker already does with `functions/utils`.
- Two checks keep `domain/` pure. ESLint has a block for `domain/**` that forbids importing `@/`, any path into `src/` or `functions/`, React and `cloudflare:` modules, and forbids `window`, `document`, `localStorage` and `navigator`. The type checks are the second guard: the site's check compiles `domain/` with the DOM library and without the Workers types, and `npm run typecheck:functions` compiles it with the Workers types and without the DOM, so code that leans on either one fails one of them. Each guard was tried with a planted file: `window` fails `typecheck:functions`, `D1Database` fails the site's check, and an import from `src/` fails the boundary test and lint.
- The lint fixture `test/unit/fixtures/lint/domain-violations.ts` breaks every rule on purpose. `eslint.config.js` ignores its folder, so `npm run lint` never counts it; the test lints its text as if it were a file in `domain/`, with the real config.
- Bundling: `npx wrangler pages functions build` succeeds before and after the change. With a temporary handler under `functions/api/` importing `../../domain/format`, the Pages Functions build bundled all five format files, and `wrangler deploy --dry-run` of a temporary daily-emails entry importing `../../../domain/format` did the same. Both temporary files were removed.

### Step 5: event-mode phases

- New `domain/events/eventMode.ts`, pure code with no database, DOM, host clock or host time zone. It exports `EventPhase` and `EVENT_PHASES` (the nine phases the brief names: `week`, `dayBefore`, `checkin`, `eventDay`, `roundPosted`, `roundInProgress`, `between`, `final`, `after`), `eventPhase(input, now)`, `phaseKey(eventId, phase, round)`, and three helpers for the WS02 endpoint and the client's window gate: `eventEndMs`, `eventModeWindow` and `firstRoundTimesFromSchedule`.
- The input is a plain object, `{ date, endDate, status, firstRoundTimes, lastRoundResultsComplete }`. `firstRoundTimes` is keyed by the event day ("YYYY-MM-DD") with that day's first `round_schedule` time ("HH:MM") or null. A null, blank or unreadable value means the day has a round whose time is not set yet. A day with no key has no round (an off day), provided at least one day of the event has a key; with no key inside the event at all, every day counts as not set. `firstRoundTimesFromSchedule(round_schedule, date, end_date)` builds it from the stored schedule (earliest time per day; a day with no round has no key only when every round is dated inside the event, otherwise each such day is null).
- Every boundary is a Louisiana wall-clock time turned into an instant with `lcaTimeToMs` (`domain/format/centralTime.ts`); the Central calendar day of `now` comes from `zonedParts` (`domain/format/date.ts`). Calendar days are counted with `Date.UTC`, so no local-time method is used. `eventEnd` is 11:59 PM on `end_date ?? date`, and the 48 hours of `after` are real elapsed time: across the November change the window closes at 10:59 PM, and across the March change at 12:59 AM.
- `phaseKey` is `${eventId}:${phase}:${round ?? 0}`, the brief's `key`. `week` and `dayBefore` come back on off days between playing days, and `checkin` and `eventDay` on each playing day, so the caller passes a round for them: the first round of the next playing day for `week` and `dayBefore` (1 before day 1), the first round of that day for `checkin` and `eventDay`. Without it, a strip hidden on the day before day 1 would stay hidden on the day before round 2. The doc comment says so and a test shows the two keys differ.
- `roundPosted`, `roundInProgress` and `between` are in the type but never returned; the doc comment says they wait for WS07's round publications and live state, when `checkin` will end at the round 1 publication and `eventDay` will stop being produced.
- Where the brief leaves a moment without a phase, the rule is under Decisions ("Event-mode phase gaps"). Where the module goes against the brief's text (`eventDay` past 11:59 PM, and `after` from 6:00 AM for an event that is not final), the rule is under Deviations ("Event-mode phase times"). The module's doc comment lists both as going beyond the brief.
- Nothing reads the module yet, so nothing visible changes and no switch is needed. WS02's endpoint, WS03's hero and WS13's event-day view import it.
- Checks: `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck:functions` and `npm run test:all` pass (unit 841 in 37 files, up from 662: 179 new, 104 in `test/unit/eventMode.test.ts`, 74 in `test/unit/eventMode-edges.test.ts` and 1 more in `domain-boundaries.test.ts` for the new file; integration 311, unchanged). Builder tests: `test/unit/eventMode.test.ts` covers every Phase 0 phase at its boundaries, midnight, both 2026 clock changes, multi-day events, days with no round, schedules with undated rounds or rounds dated outside the event, `final`, `after`, the host time zone, the key format, and that the key for the day before day 1 differs from the key for an off day before round 2 once the round is passed. Tester tests: `test/unit/eventMode-edges.test.ts` covers events that start on the clock-change Sundays, weeks that cross a clock change, the year end, the leap day, a three-day event, round times at 6:00 AM and midnight, empty and stale data, the key's three parts, and that the module imports only from `domain/format`. `npm run lint` is at 36 errors and 4 warnings, the same as before the change, none in the files this step touches.

### Step 8: sections and schedules tables

- `functions/db/schema.ts` gains three tables and two columns, nothing else changes:
  - `tournament_sections`: `id` (text, default `lower(hex(randomblob(8)))`), `tournament_id` (`ON DELETE CASCADE`), `position` (default 0), `name`, `fee_regular`, `fee_early`, `fee_late` (real, null), `cap` (integer, null), `prize_fund` (text), `rating_min`, `rating_max`, `grade_min`, `grade_max` (integer), `unrated_ok` (integer, null when the JSON does not say), `rules_set` (default 0), `prizes_json`, `extra_json`, `archived_at`, `created_at`. A null `fee_regular` means the tournament's `entry_fee`; a null `fee_early` or `fee_late` means that tier is worked out when read from the tournament's own `early_deadline`, `early_discount`, `late_after` and `late_fee`. No tier price is stored as a copy of a tournament column.
  - `tournament_schedules`: `id`, `tournament_id` (cascade), `position`, `label` (default 'Main schedule'), `time_control` (null means the tournament's own), `is_primary` (default 0), `merge_round`, `archived_at`, `created_at`.
  - `tournament_schedule_rounds`: `schedule_id` (cascade), `round`, `date`, `time`, primary key (`schedule_id`, `round`). Date and time are kept as the JSON wrote them, blank strings included.
  - `registrations.section_id` and `registrations.schedule_id`: nullable, `REFERENCES` with no `ON DELETE`, added with `ALTER TABLE ... ADD`; `registrations` is not rebuilt.
  - Indexes: unique `idx_tournament_sections_live_name` on (`tournament_id`, `name`) `WHERE archived_at IS NULL`; unique `idx_tournament_schedules_primary` on `tournament_id` `WHERE is_primary = 1 AND archived_at IS NULL`; plain indexes on both tables' `tournament_id` and on `registrations.section_id` and `schedule_id`, so a cascade or a foreign key check does not scan the table.
- `npm run db:generate -- sections schedules` wrote `migrations/0052_sections_schedules.sql` and `drizzle/meta/0001_snapshot.json`. drizzle-kit 0.31.11 wrote everything itself, the two partial unique indexes and the expression defaults included, so nothing in 0052 is hand-written and its two `ALTER TABLE ... ADD ... REFERENCES` lines need no delete action. `npm run db:generate -- sections schedules backfill --custom` then wrote the header of `0053_sections_schedules_backfill.sql`, plus `drizzle/meta/0002_snapshot.json` (the same schema as 0001) and journal entry 2. Afterwards `drizzle-kit generate` says:

  ```
  32 tables
  registrations 14 columns 4 indexes 4 fks
  tournament_schedule_rounds 4 columns 0 indexes 1 fks
  tournament_schedules 9 columns 2 indexes 1 fks
  tournament_sections 19 columns 2 indexes 1 fks
  No schema changes, nothing to migrate 😴
  ```
- `0053_sections_schedules_backfill.sql` is hand-written: four triggers (`CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS`), created first, then the backfill.
  - `tournaments_sections_sync_update`, `AFTER UPDATE OF sections, round_schedule ON tournaments`: archives live rows whose names left a valid array; brings back the latest archived row of a name that returns; adds a row for each new name (`INSERT OR IGNORE` against the partial unique index, the first of a repeated name winning); copies the JSON-shaped columns of each live row by name (`position`, `fee_regular` from a numeric `entryFee`, `prize_fund`, the rating and grade limits, `unrated_ok`, `rules_set`, `prizes_json`, and `extra_json` for any other key or a known key of an unexpected type); makes sure there is one live primary schedule; when `round_schedule` changed and is null or a valid array, replaces the primary rounds (a repeated round keeps its first entry), and fills a primary schedule that has no rounds; a `round_schedule` of JSON `'null'` (what the admin PATCH stores for `roundSchedule: null`) clears the rounds like SQL NULL and `[]`, matching the readers, which see no rounds; then fills any null `section_id` and `schedule_id` of the tournament's entries. It never writes `cap`, `fee_early`, `fee_late` or an id.
  - `tournaments_sections_sync_insert`, `AFTER INSERT ON tournaments`: sets `sections` to the value just inserted, which runs the update trigger for the new row, so the sync is written once.
  - `registrations_fill_section_insert`: a new entry without `section_id` gets the section of its name, and one without `schedule_id` the primary schedule.
  - `registrations_fill_section_update`, `AFTER UPDATE OF section ... WHEN NEW.section IS NOT OLD.section AND NEW.section_id IS OLD.section_id`: `section_id` follows the new name; a writer that sets `section_id` in the same update wins.
  - "The section of its name" is the live row of that name, else the most recently archived one; when there is none, an archived row is created, so `section_id` is never left null.
  - Every `json_each` reads its column through `json_valid` and `json_type = 'array'`; malformed JSON yields no rows, archives nothing and replaces no rounds. A plain string element is a name; an element without a text name, or with an empty one, is skipped. Names are matched exactly as stored, with no trimming, as the code matches them with `===`.
  - The backfill: `UPDATE tournaments SET sections = sections` runs the sync once for every tournament (no value in the row changes), then an archived row is added for each name a game uses that has none. Running the file again changes nothing.
- The JSON columns stay and stay authoritative. No reader changed: no runtime file reads the new tables, and none imports `functions/db`.
- `functions/db/relations.ts` gains the relations for the new foreign keys (`tournaments.tournamentSections` and `tournamentSchedules`, `tournamentSchedules.rounds`, and `registrations.sectionRow` and `scheduleRow`, named so because `registrations.section` is the name column), which `test/integration/drizzle-d1-schema.test.ts` requires for every foreign key. The schema header lists the new triggers among what it does not model. `migrations/README.md` names the 0053 triggers and the next number.
- Tests: `test/unit/migration-0053-backfill.test.ts` (23 cases) and `test/integration/sections-triggers.test.ts` (10 cases, including a refused POST and PATCH by a plain member that change no rows); edge cases in `test/unit/migration-0052-schema.test.ts` (15), `test/unit/migration-0053-edges.test.ts` (28), `test/integration/sections-triggers-edges.test.ts` (20) and `test/unit/redesign-status-k2a.test.ts` (7); `migration-safety.test.ts` gains two cases (the three new cascade children, and a later rebuild of `tournaments` would be flagged for them). - Nothing visible changes, so no switch is needed.
- **What K runs on production, read-only, before the checkpoint A merge** (`npx wrangler d1 execute lca-db --remote --command "<query>"`). Each answer is recorded here; none blocks the merge, but each row they return is a section the backfill will archive, skip or keep as found:

  ```sql
  -- 1. sections or round_schedule that is not a JSON array (each is read as no sections, or no rounds)
  SELECT id, name, substr(sections, 1, 80) AS sections FROM tournaments WHERE CASE WHEN json_valid(sections) THEN json_type(sections) <> 'array' ELSE 1 END;
  SELECT id, name, substr(round_schedule, 1, 80) AS round_schedule FROM tournaments WHERE round_schedule IS NOT NULL AND CASE WHEN json_valid(round_schedule) THEN json_type(round_schedule) <> 'array' ELSE 1 END;
  -- 2. section names given twice, missing, empty or with spaces at either end (the first of a repeated name wins; nameless ones are skipped)
  SELECT t.id, CASE e.type WHEN 'text' THEN e.value WHEN 'object' THEN json_extract(e.value, '$.name') END AS section, COUNT(*) AS times FROM tournaments t, json_each(CASE WHEN json_valid(t.sections) THEN CASE WHEN json_type(t.sections) = 'array' THEN t.sections END END) e GROUP BY t.id, section HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 OR section IS NULL OR section = '' OR section <> trim(section);
  -- 3. entries and games naming a section the JSON does not have (each name gets an archived row)
  SELECT u.tournament_id, u.section, u.source, COUNT(*) AS rows FROM (SELECT tournament_id, section, 'entry' AS source FROM registrations UNION ALL SELECT tournament_id, section, 'game' FROM tournament_games) u JOIN tournaments t ON t.id = u.tournament_id WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM json_each(CASE WHEN json_valid(t.sections) THEN CASE WHEN json_type(t.sections) = 'array' THEN t.sections END END) e WHERE CASE e.type WHEN 'text' THEN e.value WHEN 'object' THEN json_extract(e.value, '$.name') END = u.section) GROUP BY u.tournament_id, u.section, u.source;
  -- 4. entries whose tournament is gone (they cannot get a section row; expected 0)
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS entries_without_tournament FROM registrations r WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM tournaments t WHERE t.id = r.tournament_id);
  -- 5. an entryFee that is not a number (kept in extra_json; the section then charges the tournament's entry_fee in the table)
  SELECT t.id, json_extract(e.value, '$.name') AS section, json_extract(e.value, '$.entryFee') AS entry_fee FROM tournaments t, json_each(CASE WHEN json_valid(t.sections) THEN CASE WHEN json_type(t.sections) = 'array' THEN t.sections END END) e WHERE e.type = 'object' AND json_type(e.value, '$.entryFee') NOT IN ('integer', 'real', 'null');
  ```
- **On merge:** `.github/workflows/migrate-db.yml` applies 0052 and 0053 to production (`lca-db --remote`) when checkpoint A merges to `main`. Both only add: three tables, two nullable columns, indexes and triggers, and the backfill writes only the new tables and columns (its `UPDATE tournaments SET sections = sections` rewrites each row with its own value), so the code already deployed keeps working. K migrates the preview database separately (`npm run db:migrate:preview`, ordering rule 2).
- **What K runs on production after the merge, and again before checkpoint B merges** (all expected 0):

  ```sql
  SELECT COUNT(*) FROM registrations WHERE section_id IS NULL;
  SELECT COUNT(*) FROM registrations WHERE schedule_id IS NULL;
  SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tournaments t WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tournament_schedules p WHERE p.tournament_id = t.id AND p.is_primary = 1 AND p.archived_at IS NULL) <> 1;
  SELECT COUNT(*) FROM registrations r JOIN tournament_sections s ON s.id = r.section_id WHERE s.name <> r.section OR s.tournament_id <> r.tournament_id;
  ```
  The queries were checked on a local database built from the migrations with rows of every kind above. Results on production, Monday, October 12, 2026 (read-only, after 0052 and 0053 were applied): all four returned 0. Production then held 1 tournament (a test event, status active), 15 entries, 3 live section rows and no archived ones, and the six triggers `members_role_insert`, `members_role_update`, `registrations_fill_section_insert`, `registrations_fill_section_update`, `tournaments_sections_sync_insert` and `tournaments_sections_sync_update`.

### Step 9: one writer for sections

- `domain/events/sections.ts` (no zod): `LegacySection` (an element of the JSON), `SectionInput` (what a save takes: the legacy keys plus an optional `id`, `cap` and `fees { early, late }`), `SectionRecord` (a row read back); `normalizeLegacySections` (column text or a parsed value; a plain string is a name, an element without a text name is skipped, the first of a repeated name wins, nothing trimmed, as the 0053 trigger reads it); `toLegacySection` (the JSON element: the keys the admin sent (known keys first, then any others, as zod returns them, so the stored text can reorder keys; contents are unchanged), without `id`, `cap`, `fees` or undefined values; a bare name stays a bare name); `SectionListItem` and `asSectionInput` (a list element a request sends is a section or a bare name, which is the section `{ name }`); the known keys of `LegacySection` are typed `unknown`, because events saved earlier can hold one of another type; `repeatedSectionName`, `sectionListProblem` and the decision 7 messages; `tierFees(section, tournament)` (regular is `fee_regular` else the tournament's `entry_fee`; early and late are the section's own price, else regular less `early_discount` when `early_deadline` is set and regular plus `late_fee` when `late_after` is set, as checkout prices them; null when the event has no such price).
- `domain/contracts/events.ts`: `sectionSchema` (a section in a request: name 1 to 80 characters and not blank, `cap` a positive whole number or null, the rule and prize fields, optional `id` and `fees`, other keys kept; a known key whose value is of its column's type must be valid for the column, and a value of another type is taken as it is and kept in `extra_json`, as the 0053 trigger keeps it), `sectionListItemSchema` (a list element: a section, or a bare name of 1 to 80 characters, so the manage page can send back a stored list of names with the sections it adds), `savedSectionSchema` (a section in an answer), `adminTournamentSchema` (every `tournaments` column, sections from the table) and its response, and the loose request schemas for the admin create and edit. `registry.ts` adds `'admin/tournaments'` POST and `'admin/tournaments/[id]'` PATCH; `test/unit/contracts-pending.ts` drops both lines and `PENDING_COUNT` goes from 123 to 121.
- `functions/utils/events/sectionsRepo.ts`, the first runtime use of `getDb`:
  - `loadSections(db, tournamentId, { includeArchived })` (live rows by position, then archived ones, latest first) and `loadSectionsFor(db, ids)` (90 ids per `IN` list, under D1's 100 bound parameters).
  - `buildSaveSections(db, tournamentId, input, { reportSettings })` returns the queries for one `db.batch`, or the reason in words. `input` can mix sections and bare names; a bare name is the section `{ name }` and stays a bare name in the JSON. It matches by id (an id that is not this event's is refused), else the live row of that name, else the latest archived row of that name (which comes back), else a new row with an id made in code (16 hex characters from `crypto.randomUUID`). Order: archive the sections left out; give every live row being renamed a temporary name (longer than any allowed name and holding its id); give each section its final name, position and fields, or insert it; move entries of renamed rows by `section_id`, then games and the `report_settings.sections` key by old name (games in two steps, so a swap does not mix them); write `tournaments.sections` last. Leaving `cap` or a fee out keeps the row's value; null clears it.
  - `columnsFromLegacy` works out the row's columns from the JSON element exactly as the 0053 trigger does (a known key only when its type is the expected one, the rest in `extra_json`), so the trigger finds nothing to change.
  - Decision 7: a section left out that has entries that are not withdrawn (waitlisted ones count), or games, refuses the save with its message; nothing is written.
  - Guards: the plan is made from rows read before the batch, so the batch opens with guard statements that fail it as a whole when the plan has gone stale. One compares the rows as read (id, name and `archived_at` of each, by id) with the table as it is when the batch runs; the others check, in lists cut like the reads, that no section being archived has gained an entry that is not withdrawn or a game. A guard raises an error only when its condition holds (`json_extract` with a malformed path, selected from the tournament row), and the error rolls the whole batch back. `isSectionsConflict` recognises that error and the live-name index refusing a name another save just took. A guard is a select builder, because Drizzle's D1 batch cannot bind the parameters of a raw `db.run(sql)` query.
  - `runBatch`, `saveSections` (plan and run alone) and `sectionResponse` (a row priced with `tierFees` for an answer).
- `functions/api/admin/tournaments/[id].ts` PATCH: reads the body with `parseBody` and the new contract, loads the tournament and writes its columns through Drizzle, and puts that `UPDATE` (which no longer writes `sections`) and the writer's queries in one `db.batch`. Role checks are unchanged and come before any write: `requireTournamentManager`, then only an LCA admin may change the organizing club. `sections: null` or no `sections` leaves the sections alone. When the batch fails because the sections changed under it (a guard, or another save taking a name), nothing is written, the tournament's own columns included, and it answers 409 with `{ error: "These sections changed while you were saving. Reload the page and try again." }`; any other failure is rethrown. It answers every column with the live sections from the table.
- `functions/api/admin/tournaments.ts` POST: `parseBody` with the new contract; the `INSERT` (sections left to the column default, `'[]'`) and the writer's queries in one `db.batch`, with the same 409 for a conflict; it answers every column with the sections from the table, ids included. The wizard reads only `id`. The handlers keep their own messages for missing fields and an unknown status.
- `test/integration/factories.ts`: `seedTournament` inserts the row without sections and then saves them through the writer (plain string sections are names).
- The 0053 triggers stay. The update trigger fires on the writer's JSON write and changes nothing (proved by running each plan in two batches); the entry trigger fires when a rename moves `registrations.section` and resolves to the same row. When old code writes only the JSON (the deploy window), the trigger still makes the rows follow.
- The site is unchanged: today's setup form sends no ids, so its sections match by name.
- Nothing visible changes apart from the refusals (repeated names, removing a section with entries or games), which are data rules and come with no switch.
- Tests: `test/unit/sections-writer-audit.test.ts` (5), `test/unit/sections-domain.test.ts` (27), `test/integration/sections-writer.test.ts` (42, among them a plan gone stale under another save, a late entry and a late game on a section being removed, and a PATCH whose rows change just before its batch, answered 409 with nothing written) and `test/integration/contracts/admin-tournaments.test.ts` (16, among them a PATCH that sends back a stored list of bare names and an old element with its price as text, with a section added). `schema-drift.test.ts` loses its import check (one case), and `sections-triggers.test.ts` and `sections-triggers-edges.test.ts` follow decision 7 and the new POST answer (see Deviations). `tournament-create.test.ts` and `tournament-edit.test.ts` pass unchanged, including the `toEqual` on the parsed JSON at `tournament-edit.test.ts:122`.

- `domain/registration/pricing.ts` gains `priceEntry(section, tournament, nowMs, { isLcaMember })`, with no storage in it. `section` is a section as `loadSections` returns it (`feeRegular`, `feeEarly`, `feeLate`), and `tournament` carries `entry_fee`, `early_deadline`, `early_discount`, `late_after`, `late_fee` and, until step 15, `member_discount`, taken from the tournament row the request reads, so changing one of those columns changes the next price at once. It answers the same `{ amount, base, lines }` as before, with the same labels ("Early entry discount", "LCA member discount", "Late entry fee") and the same sum: the base (`fee_regular`, else `entry_fee`), less the early discount while the early deadline has not passed, less the member discount for an active member, plus the late fee after the late date, rounded to the cent and never below zero, with lines only when the base is above zero. A section's own `fee_early` or `fee_late` (none exist until WS08) replaces the worked-out line under the same label, its amount being the difference from the base. `entryPrice(t, sectionName, opts)` stays for the tournament page and the family entry panel until step 13: it reads the legacy JSON through `normalizeLegacySections` and hands the section to `priceEntry`. `PricedTournament` keeps `sections`; the new `PriceTournament` is the same without it.

### Step 13: the pages read the section rows

- `src/lib/api.ts` takes its tournament types from the contracts with `import type` (a runtime import would put zod in the site bundle): `ApiTournamentSection` is `SavedSection` (`savedSectionSchema`: `id`, `name`, `entryFee`, the rules, `rulesSet`, `cap`, `fees { regular, early, late }`, plus the optional `prizeFund`, `unratedOk` and `prizes` and any stored extra key), `ApiTournamentListItem` is `TournamentListItem`, and `ApiTournamentDetail` is the detail answer's tournament with `custom_details` and `round_schedule` typed as the setup form writes them and `waitlist_count` optional (only the event page gets it). A new `ApiSectionDraft` is a section while the wizard or the manage page edits it: a loaded one keeps its id, one added in the form has only a name and a fee. `adminCreateTournament` and `adminUpdateTournament` take `ApiSectionDraft[]`; `SectionRulesEditor` and `PrizesEditor` take and return one.
- The manage page keeps every loaded section object while it is edited (fee, prize fund, rules, prizes) and sends the list back whole when it changed, ids included, so the server matches each section by id. It already sent what it loaded; the type now carries the id, so nothing can drop it. A section added on the page has no id until the save. The wizard's "From an existing tournament" copy drops the source's ids (the create ignores them anyway); a wizard section from scratch is `{ name, entryFee }` as before. Neither screen has a box to rename a section today, so the rename path is the body the page sends with a name changed (see the test below).
- The tournament page and the family entry panel price with `priceShownSection(section, tournament, nowMs, { isLcaMember })`, new in `domain/registration/pricing.ts` (zod-free, next to `priceEntry`), with the section found by name, as before. An answer's `fees.early` and `fees.late` are either the section's own price or one worked out from the tournament's columns (`tierFees`), and checkout prices the two differently: an own price replaces the line's amount, a worked-out one keeps the tournament's discount or fee, and a worked-out early price is clamped at $0 where the discount line is not. So the helper works out what the tournament alone would give and passes a tier price on to `priceEntry` as the section's own only when it differs. The page then shows what checkout charges for a section with its own early or late price, and the same lines as before for every other section (no section has its own tier price until WS08). The one case the answer cannot tell apart is an own early price of $0 where the early discount is larger than the fee: it is read as worked out, and differs from checkout only when the late fee is also due. A name with no section (nothing chosen yet) is priced at the event fee, as `entryPrice` priced it. The member discount still applies until step 15. ### Step 14: schedules have one writer and one reader

- `domain/events/schedules.ts` (no zod) holds `normalizeRoundSchedule` (reads the old JSON the way the 0053 trigger does), `roundScheduleJson` (writes `[{ round, date, time }]`), `validateSchedules(schedules, roundCount)`, `roundsFor(schedules, scheduleId)` and `scheduleForRound`. Rules: exactly one primary; a second schedule's merge round is from 2 to the event's round count and it lists exactly rounds 1 to merge round minus 1; the primary lists the rest; rounds are unique within a schedule; names are unique. `roundsFor` gives a player on the second schedule their own rounds before the merge round and the primary's from the merge round on.
- `domain/contracts/events.ts` adds `scheduleRoundSchema`, `scheduleSchema` and `scheduleInputSchema` (types `ScheduleRound`, `Schedule`, `ScheduleRequest`). Every tournament answer types `round_schedule` with the round schema and gains `schedules`; the admin PATCH body accepts `schedules`. `src/lib/api.ts` takes `ApiRoundScheduleItem` and the new `ApiSchedule` from the contracts with `import type`. No page file changed, and `npm run check:bundle` still finds no zod (114 files).
- `functions/utils/events/schedulesRepo.ts` provides `loadSchedules`, `loadSchedulesFor` (one query per 90 event ids, at most 100 bound parameters), `scheduleResponse`, `roundScheduleResponse` and `buildSaveSchedules`. The 0053 insert trigger already makes a primary schedule for every event, so the writer matches that row (a primary sent without an id matches the existing primary) and does not create another. Batch order: guards, archive the schedules left out, demote the old primary, update or insert rows (new ids made in code), rewrite changed rounds, then the `round_schedule` JSON last, in today's shape. A new primary is only inserted after the old one is archived or demoted, because the partial unique index allows one live primary per event. The save takes either `roundSchedule` (today's body field) or `schedules` (the whole list); sending both is 400.
- The admin PATCH (`functions/api/admin/tournaments/[id].ts`) runs the schedule plan after the sections plan in the same batch, with the same kind of in-batch guard (a fingerprint of the event's schedule rows, a check that a schedule being removed has no entries that are not withdrawn, and a check that every live second schedule's merge round fits `tournaments.rounds` as the batch runs). A stale plan is 409 with a plain message. The main update no longer writes `round_schedule`.
- Readers: `round_schedule` is the live primary's rounds, as a list, and `schedules[]` holds the live rows, in `functions/api/tournaments/[id].ts`, `functions/api/admin/tournaments/[id]/manage.ts`, the admin PATCH and POST answers, the registration PATCH answer and the list in `functions/api/tournaments.ts`. `toTournamentResponse` now requires the schedule records and no longer parses the column.
- Registrations keep `schedule_id` from the 0053 trigger (the primary schedule) until WS06 adds the schedule picker. A second schedule has no screen until WS08's setup, so the new refusals below have no flag.
- Tests: `schedules-audit.test.ts` (11), `schedules-domain.test.ts` (31) and `schedules.test.ts` (46), all new, plus 3 cases in `contracts/tournaments.test.ts`. `tournaments-list-edges.test.ts` and `contracts-layer.test.ts` now count the `schedules` field. `tournament-edit.test.ts`, `sections-writer.test.ts` and the lifecycle tests pass unchanged. `contracts-pending.ts` stays at 110: no new route.
- From review: a save that does not send `rounds` leaves the round count out of its update (it used to write back the count it had read), so it cannot undo a count another save changed. The merge-round fit guard reads `tournaments.rounds` inside the batch and runs whenever a save sends schedules or a round count; a save that sends neither has no schedule statement. Two races are covered by tests: a round-count change landing between a schedule save's read and its batch, and a second schedule added while a round-count change is being checked. Both end in 409 with the data still valid.
- Checks: `npm run build`, `npm run check:bundle`, `npm run typecheck:functions` and `npm run test:all` pass (unit 1395 in 61 files, up from 1352 in 59; integration 725 in 55 files, up from 674 in 54). `npm run lint` is 34 errors and 4 warnings before and after; no touched file has an error. `npx wrangler pages functions build` compiles. `scanner:check` was not run; nothing under `scanner/` or `functions/utils/scan/` changed. Nothing was run against a remote database.

### Step 15: no member pricing, and the LCA membership requirement

- **One price.** `priceEntry(section, tournament, nowMs)` and `priceShownSection(section, tournament, nowMs)` in `domain/registration/pricing.ts` lost their fourth argument. The "LCA member discount" line and `PriceTournament.member_discount` are gone. Regular, early and late come from the section row and the live tournament columns as before, so a member and a non-member entering the same section at the same moment pay the same in every tier, even when `member_discount` is above 0 in the row. `functions/api/registrations.ts`, `registrations/batch.ts` and `admin/tournaments/[id]/waitlist.ts` price without member status. `registrations/[id].ts` never used the member discount and did not change. Their SQL did not change, so under the Drizzle conversion rule nothing converted; the `membership_status` selects in `batch.ts` and `waitlist.ts` stay, unused.
- **Migration `0054_requires_lca_membership.sql`**, generated with `npm run db:generate -- requires lca membership`: `ALTER TABLE tournaments ADD requires_lca_membership integer DEFAULT 1 NOT NULL`. After a statement breakpoint, one data statement added by hand, as the header says: `UPDATE tournaments SET requires_lca_membership = 0 WHERE club_id IS NOT NULL AND requires_lca_membership <> 0`, so existing club-run events start with the requirement off. A second run changes nothing, and the header warns that it must not be run by hand once a club has switched the requirement on (wrangler runs each migration once). The update fires no trigger: the only update trigger on `tournaments` watches `sections` and `round_schedule`. `member_discount` stays in the table, unread and no longer written, so no data is dropped. `drizzle/meta/_journal.json` has its fourth entry and `drizzle/meta/0003_snapshot.json` differs from the previous snapshot only by the new column. `migrations/README.md` says `0055` is next and gains a short section on adding a data statement after a generated change, with 0054 as the example. `drizzle-kit generate` afterwards reports "No schema changes, nothing to migrate". 0054 was applied to the local D1 only (`wrangler d1 migrations apply lca-db --local`).
- **The rule.** `domain/membership/requirement.ts` (no zod, no imports): `requiresLcaMembership(tournament, { forceAll? })` is true for an LCA-run event (`club_id` null) whatever the column says, otherwise the column, or true when `FORCE_LCA_MEMBERSHIP` is on; `hasActiveMembershipOn(player, date)`; `needsMembershipAtCheckout(player, tournament)`, true when the event requires it and the player has no active membership on the event date, for WS06 to call; and `LCA_RUN_NEEDS_MEMBERSHIP`, the plain 400 message. `FORCE_LCA_MEMBERSHIP` is a constant, off today. Brief decision D12 plans an admin-only site setting `membership_required_for_all`, built with the site settings in WS08, that replaces the constant; the module's comment says so.
- **Who may set it** (decision 5 as applied). On `PATCH /api/admin/tournaments/[id]`, a body carrying `requiresLcaMembership` is accepted from an LCA admin, or from a club rep whose club is the event's club. An assigned director, who manages the event through `canManageTournament` but is neither, gets 403, even when sending the value the event already has; so do another club's rep (assigned or not), a rep assigned to an LCA-run event and a plain member. All checks run before any write. Sending false when the event will have no club after the save is 400 ("An LCA membership is always required for an event LCA runs. Only a club-run event can switch it off."). Taking the club off an event forces the column to 1, and every save of an event with no club writes 1. Otherwise the column is written only when sent, so a stale edit cannot undo another save's change. `POST /api/admin/tournaments` stores 0 for a new event with a club and 1 otherwise, unless the body says otherwise, and the false-with-no-club case is 400. Both writes go into the existing Drizzle `set()` and `insert`. Both endpoints accept `memberDiscount` and drop it, so the current setup form and older clients keep working.
- **Contracts.** `domain/contracts/events.ts`: the tournament row schema gains `requires_lca_membership` (so the list, detail, manage and admin answers carry it); the create and edit requests gain `requiresLcaMembership: z.boolean().optional()`; `memberDiscount` stays in the edit request, marked as accepted and ignored. `contracts-pending.ts` is unchanged (no new route). `functions/types.ts`: `TournamentRow.requires_lca_membership`; `functions/db/schema.ts` gains the column and a "retired" comment on `memberDiscount`. `src/lib/api.ts` drops `memberDiscount` and gains an optional `requiresLcaMembership` on the create and update bodies.
- **Pages.** The member-discount input is gone from `TournamentManagePage.tsx` (state, loading and sending), the discount grid goes from three columns to two, and the label "Discounts and late fee" reads "Early-entry discount and late fee". `TournamentDetailPage.tsx` drops the "LCA members save $X" line, the member price line, `isLcaMember` and the `selfIsLcaMember` prop. `FamilyRegistrationPanel.tsx` prices each player by section only (`Player.isLcaMember` and the `selfIsLcaMember` prop are gone). `HomePage.tsx` no longer lists "discounted tournament entry" as a membership benefit; it reads "entry to LCA-run tournaments across the state". These removals ship without a switch (see Deviations).
- **The setup switch.** A checkbox on the Registration tab, "Players need a current LCA membership to enter", with its state in words below ("Required: ..." or "Not required: ..."), behind the new switch `membershipRequirementSwitch` in `src/lib/features.ts` (off). It is drawn only when the switch is on, the event has a club, and the viewer is an LCA admin or the rep of that club. The page sends `requiresLcaMembership` only when its value changed, so an assigned director saving other settings never meets the 403. **Leave `membershipRequirementSwitch` off until WS06 enforces the rule at checkout**: the state text says every player must hold a membership, and until then a non-member can still enter. The flag's comment in `src/lib/features.ts` says the same.
- **Every tournament answer gives `member_discount` 0 (checkpoint B review).** `toTournamentResponse` in `functions/utils/events/sectionsRepo.ts` answers `member_discount: 0` for every tournament, whatever the stored column holds, which stays unchanged. Why: browser tabs opened before the deploy still run the old site code, which subtracts the answered member discount from a member's price. With the real value in the answer, those tabs would keep showing the member price while Stripe charges the one price. With 0 they show what Stripe charges. Every answer that carries a whole tournament row goes through this function (public list and detail, admin manage, create, edit and registration edit); the other answers select named columns without it, and registration, batch registration and waitlist read the row only inside. The contract still passes, since 0 is a valid dollar amount. `test/unit/no-member-price-surface.test.ts` now allows exactly that one line in `sectionsRepo.ts`, and `test/integration/pricing-no-member-discount.test.ts` shows an event stored with 5 answering 0 on the public detail (signed out and signed in), the public list and admin manage, with the column still 5. The same review fixed the frozen price time (see Deviations, step 13).
- **Not done here.** Nothing refuses or charges a non-member at checkout, because today's registration has no way to add a membership inline and refusing would leave non-members with no way forward. That, and the schedule picker, are WS06's. The full setup toggle with its fee ladder is WS08's.

  - 0054 must reach production before the deploy of this step, or with it. The event edit reads `requires_lca_membership` and the event create writes it, so without 0054 in production every event edit and every event creation would answer 500. `migrate-db.yml` applies it on the merge to `main`, in seconds, while the Pages build takes minutes. If that run fails, the merge is not finished until it is re-run and passes.

### Checkpoint B: steps 9 to 15

**Merged into `main` as `748a5ef` on Monday, October 12, 2026 at 10:29 PM UTC** (pull request 104, a merge commit on head `b41ac45`). `migrate-db.yml` applied 0054 to production at 10:29:51 PM UTC on its first attempt; `d1_migrations` now ends at `0054_requires_lca_membership.sql`. The Pages production build and the daily-emails worker deploy both succeeded. The post-deploy query for club events with the requirement on returned no rows (production has no club-run event), and the one LCA-run event has it on. The public site answered afterwards; its only event is hidden, so there was no public row to inspect. Checkpoint B moves tournament sections and schedules off their JSON columns and onto the tables checkpoint A created, then removes member pricing.

- **Step 9:** one writer for sections (`sectionsRepo.ts`), rename by id, the refusal to remove a section that has entries or games, 409 when a save raced another, and the first Drizzle use in the admin tournament create and edit.
- **Step 10:** player registration (single, family and entry edit) reads the section rows, sets `section_id` itself, refuses archived sections, and answers malformed bodies with `{ error, fields }`.

- **Step 12:** every server answer that carries a tournament reads sections from the table and gains `id`, `cap` and `fees`; `round_schedule` is answered as a list.

- **Step 14:** one writer and one reader for schedules, `schedules[]` in every tournament answer, and new 400 and 409 refusals for schedule edits.
- **Step 15:** no member price anywhere, `requires_lca_membership` (migration 0054) and who may set it.
- **Migrations in this checkpoint:** 0054 only (0052 and 0053 belong to checkpoint A). It adds one column and one idempotent update, and drops nothing.
- **Visible to people without a switch:**
  - One price for everyone: an active LCA member pays the same as a non-member in every section and tier (single entry, family entry and waitlist offers). On an event with a member discount, a member's Stripe charge goes up by that discount. Non-member amounts are unchanged.
  - The event page no longer shows "LCA members save $X on entry. Join LCA" or the "LCA member discount" line in the price box and the confirmation dialog. The section list and the family panel show one price per section.
  - The setup page (Registration tab) no longer has the "LCA member discount ($)" box. The label "Discounts and late fee" reads "Early-entry discount and late fee", with two boxes to a row.
  - The home page membership blurb "including discounted tournament entry, your official membership profile, and access to events across the state" now reads "including entry to LCA-run tournaments across the state and your official membership profile".
  - New plain refusals when editing an event: a section with entries or paired games cannot be removed; two sections cannot share a name; schedule edits have new refusals; simultaneous saves get "These sections changed while you were saving. Reload the page and try again."
  - The US Chess rating report includes players entered under a section later removed; its messages say "US Chess" and show weekday dates; an event whose report downloaded cleanly can be blocked until those players have US Chess IDs.
  - Registration and walk-in refusals say "US Chess ID"; the membership-expiry warning shows the weekday (for example "Tue, Sep 1, 2026"); a badly formed request gets "Some fields are missing or not valid."
  - A section saved without a fee of its own (very old events only) now shows the event fee instead of "Free", and the event fee is written into it the first time its sections are saved. No price changes.
  - A "Players need a current LCA membership to enter" switch exists on the setup page, hidden behind `membershipRequirementSwitch` (off). Nothing checks membership at checkout yet.

At the end of step 15 the counts were unit 1447 and integration 787. `scanner:check` was not run; nothing under `scanner/` or `functions/utils/scan/` changed.
- **Before the merge: every query below was run on production on Monday, October 12, 2026** (`npx wrangler d1 execute lca-db --remote --command "<query>"`, read-only, one statement per command, from the cloud session with the LCA account's token). Production then held 1 tournament ("Test Tournament Name Sept 2026", status active, no club) and 15 entries. Results: the member-discount query returned no rows; the four step 8 queries each returned 0; every legacy-shape query returned no rows. Nothing blocks the merge on the data.
  1. The member-discount query. A row means an open event has a member discount. After the deploy a member pays full price, and tabs still running the old code would keep showing the member price (the server now answers 0, see Step 15, so they show the true price). K accepts that before merging.

     ```sql
     SELECT id, name, member_discount FROM tournaments WHERE member_discount > 0 AND status != 'completed';
     ```
  2. The four step 8 queries again (0052 and 0053 are applied). Each expects 0.
  3. Legacy-shape checks, each expected to return no rows.

     Saves that would now be refused (a section name over 80 characters or blank, a negative fee, prizes stored as a list, or a custom detail that is not a title and body). A row is an event whose next save would be locked out with the generic message:

     ```sql
     SELECT tournament_id, name FROM tournament_sections WHERE archived_at IS NULL AND (length(name) > 80 OR trim(name) = '' OR fee_regular < 0 OR json_type(prizes_json) = 'array');
     SELECT t.id FROM tournaments t, json_each(CASE WHEN json_valid(t.custom_details) AND json_type(t.custom_details)='array' THEN t.custom_details END) e WHERE e.type <> 'object' OR json_type(e.value,'$.title') IS NOT 'text' OR json_type(e.value,'$.body') IS NOT 'text';
     ```

     Price or display changed by wrong-typed keys. A row is a section whose stored extra keys could change its price, prize fund, rules or rating limits on the new pages:

     ```sql
     SELECT tournament_id, name, extra_json FROM tournament_sections WHERE archived_at IS NULL AND json_valid(extra_json) AND (json_type(extra_json,'$.entryFee') IS NOT NULL OR json_type(extra_json,'$.prizeFund') IS NOT NULL OR json_type(extra_json,'$.rulesSet') IS NOT NULL OR json_type(extra_json,'$.unratedOk') IS NOT NULL OR json_type(extra_json,'$.ratingMax') IS NOT NULL OR json_type(extra_json,'$.ratingMin') IS NOT NULL);
     ```

     "Free" becomes the event fee. A row is a section with no fee of its own on an event that has a fee, which will now show and charge the event fee:

     ```sql
     SELECT s.tournament_id, s.name, t.entry_fee FROM tournament_sections s JOIN tournaments t ON t.id = s.tournament_id WHERE s.archived_at IS NULL AND s.fee_regular IS NULL AND t.entry_fee > 0;
     ```

     Waitlist and move repricing for removed sections. A row is a removed section that still has live entries and a fee, whose waitlist offers or moves would be priced from it:

     ```sql
     SELECT s.tournament_id, s.name, s.fee_regular, COUNT(*) FROM tournament_sections s JOIN registrations r ON r.section_id = s.id WHERE s.archived_at IS NOT NULL AND s.fee_regular IS NOT NULL AND r.withdrawn_at IS NULL GROUP BY s.id;
     ```

     JSON and table parity. A row is an event whose live section rows do not match the sections in its old JSON column (rows where a name is repeated in the JSON can be ignored):

     ```sql
     SELECT t.id FROM tournaments t WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tournament_sections s WHERE s.tournament_id = t.id AND s.archived_at IS NULL) <> (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT json_extract(e.value,'$.name')) + COUNT(DISTINCT CASE e.type WHEN 'text' THEN e.value END) FROM json_each(CASE WHEN json_valid(t.sections) AND json_type(t.sections)='array' THEN t.sections END) e WHERE COALESCE(CASE e.type WHEN 'text' THEN e.value WHEN 'object' THEN json_extract(e.value,'$.name') END,'') <> '');
     ```
- **Merging checkpoint B** (done as recorded above; the notes below stay for the record and for a rollback).
  - Merge when no event is running and no director is editing.

That covers Details, Registration pricing and visibility, Schedule, Start or Finish event, US Chess upload settings and the admin page's club change. On the real database, club-run events may fail too. Nothing is half-written, because each save is one batch. Player registration, family entry, walk-ins, waitlist offers, check-in and the public pages keep working.

After the deploy run `SELECT id, name FROM tournaments WHERE club_id IS NOT NULL AND requires_lca_membership = 1;`. If it returns rows, run 0054's UPDATE again. That is safe while the switch is off and no club has turned it on.

### Step 16: server helpers grouped by area

Checkpoint C (steps 16 to 19) moves files and changes nothing else. This step moves the server helpers; `functions/api` stays where it is, because its paths are the URLs.

- **The tools.** `scripts/move-files.ts <map.json> [--dry-run]` (run with `node --no-warnings --experimental-strip-types`, like the other TypeScript scripts) runs `git mv` for each entry and rewrites every specifier that reaches a moved file, in every code file under `src`, `functions`, `workers`, `domain`, `test`, `scripts` and `scanner` and at the root: static imports, export-from, `import()`, `typeof import()`, `vi.mock`, `vi.doMock`, `vi.unmock`, `vi.doUnmock`, `vi.importActual`, `vi.importMock` and `require`, keeping a `?raw` query, a `@/` or `@domain/` alias and the specifier's own form (no extension, the file's extension, `.js` for a `.ts` file, or a folder for its index). A moved file's own relative imports of files that stay are rewritten too. Each specifier is resolved with `ts.resolveModuleName` and the options and paths of `tsconfig.app.json` (`tsconfig.functions.json` has no paths); a `.sql`, `.md`, `.css` or `.json` target is resolved as a path. Every new specifier is resolved again against the layout after the move and must reach the same file. Any relative or alias specifier that cannot be resolved stops the run with exit code 1, before anything is moved or written; `--dry-run` prints the plan and the problems. `scripts/verify-move.ts <map.json>` checks the result against git: every file in the map is a rename (`git diff -M`), and in the moved files and every other changed file each changed line is a specifier line that is the same once its specifiers are blanked out, or a line whose only change is a moved path written out in a comment or string. It lists both kinds line by line, so a reviewer can read them separately.
- **The map,** `scripts/moves/server-areas.json`:
  - `events/`: `tournament-manage`, `prizes`, `champions` and `linkPreview`, beside `sectionsRepo` and `schedulesRepo`, which were already there.
  - `registration/`: `registrationEmails` and `registrationOpenNotify`.
  - `membership/`: `membershipActivation`, `membershipExpiry` and `ratingSnapshots`.
  - `live/swiss/`: the swiss folder whole (`engine`, `matching`, `tiebreaks` and their three tests).
  - `admin/`: `audit`, `campaigns`, `tickets`, `permissions` and `members`.
  - At the root, unchanged: the platform files (`auth`, `response`, `json`, `csv`, `email`, `emailLayout`, `site`, `supabase`, `stripe`, `uscf`, `posts`), the four one-line re-exports of `domain/` (`pricing`, `sectionRules`, `regions`, `time`), and `family.ts` (see Deviations). `scan/` is untouched, so the scanner's own checks are not set off.
- **The run.** `--dry-run` on the map: 15 entries (20 files), 90 specifiers in 63 files, 462 files searched, 0 that could not be resolved. Applied, then `verify-move` against the commit before the move, with `--ignore REDESIGN_STATUS.md` because this record changes in the same commit: 20 renames (19 specifier lines and 17 path mentions inside them), 59 other files (71 specifier lines and 13 path mentions), nothing else. The path mentions are the moved files' header comments, comments that name a moved file (`tournament-manage.ts`, `generate-pairings.ts`, `support.ts`, the daily-emails worker, `src/lib/api.ts`, `src/pages/AdminEmailPage.tsx` and `domain/contracts/events.ts`), the swiss include in `vitest.config.ts`, and the path strings in three tests (see Deviations).

From `workers/daily-emails`, `npx wrangler deploy --dry-run` needs no account either: 31.96 KiB before and 31.99 KiB after, and the bundles differ only in three path comments. `tsc -p workers/daily-emails/tsconfig.json` passes with its include unchanged.

### Step 18: API client split by area

The third of checkpoint C's moves. The site's API client, `src/lib/api.ts` (2176 lines), is split into one module per area plus the shared request helpers; `src/lib/api.ts` becomes a barrel, so every importer of `@/lib/api` sees the same names and no importer changed.

- **The tool.** `scripts/split-api.ts` (run with `node --no-warnings --experimental-strip-types`, like the other scripts) parses `src/lib/api.ts` with the TypeScript compiler and moves each top-level declaration by its source text, with the comments above it, to the module the map names, keeping the declarations' order. Each module gets a header comment and the imports its declarations use: the original imports (`@/lib/supabase` in `http.ts`, the `RawScan` type in `live`, the five contract types in `events` with the comment above that import), `authHeaders` and `handleResponse` from `@/lib/http`, and with `import type` the types another area owns, from that area's `api.ts`. It stops, writing nothing, when the file declares a name the map lacks or the map names one the file lacks, on a statement kind it does not move, a comment that would be left behind, a private helper of one area used by another, an import of an area from `http.ts`, or a cycle between areas. `--dry-run` prints the counts per module and the imports each gets. `--check` reads the result: the barrel holds only export-from lines and exports exactly the names in `test/unit/fixtures/api-exports.json`, each through one line; each of those names is exported by one module only; each module declares exactly the names the map gives it; no area module imports `src/lib/api.ts`, `http.ts` imports no area and no area `index.ts` re-exports `api.ts`. `--compare <rev>` adds the byte check against `src/lib/api.ts` as it was at that commit.
- **The map,** `scripts/moves/api-split.json`: a JSON object of name to target, in the order of the old file, naming all 185 top-level declarations (182 exports and the private helpers `authHeaders`, `handleResponse` and `exportQuery`). Summarised under Decisions, "API client by area".
- **The fixtures, taken first.** From the unsplit file, before anything else changed: `test/unit/fixtures/api-exports.json`, the 182 exported names (117 functions, the class `ApiError`, 54 interfaces and 10 type aliases), read from the syntax and from the TypeScript checker, which agreed; and `test/unit/fixtures/api-fetch-paths.json`, the 77 distinct paths route-audit extracts (the regex matches 122 times on 104 lines).
- **The run.** `--dry-run`: 185 declarations into 9 modules, 0 problems. Applied, then `--check --compare bb92e90`: 182 names through the barrel, the same set as the snapshot, each in one module; 185 declarations (64,142 characters) equal byte for byte; the rest of the old file is its 3 import statements and 1 newline. Running the script again on the old file in an empty folder writes the same ten files byte for byte.
  - `src/lib/http.ts`: 3 (`authHeaders`, `ApiError`, `handleResponse`).
  - `src/areas/events/api.ts`: 49. `registration`: 14. `households`: 5. `live`: 8. `membership`: 19, plus the private `exportQuery`. `clubs`: 20. `admin`: 34. `governance`: 32.
- **The byte check, a second way.** Separately from the script: each module's text after its last import line, cut into statements, put back in the old order and joined, equals the old file after its first 7 lines (the header and the imports) once blank lines are left out of both (1,962 lines, no difference). The only differences are blank lines between declarations: two blank lines become one, a line holding only a space becomes empty, and `AnnouncementTone` and `AnnouncementSize`, which had no blank line between them, now have one.
- **`http.ts` keeps its helpers' text.** `authHeaders` and `handleResponse` were private; the area modules need them, so `http.ts` ends with `export { authHeaders, handleResponse }` rather than gaining an `export` keyword on each. The barrel re-exports only `ApiError` from it (`export { ApiError } from '@/lib/http'`), so the two helpers do not become new names on `@/lib/api`.
- **The barrel.** `src/lib/api.ts` is a header comment, `export { ApiError } from '@/lib/http'` and `export * from` each of the eight area modules. The three tests that `vi.mock('@/lib/api')` spread the original module first (`tournament-manage-membership-switch`, `tournament-manage-no-member-discount` and `tournament-pages-pricing`) and pass unchanged, as do `api-section-bodies.test.ts` (which imports `@/lib/api` after mocking `@/lib/supabase`; `http.ts` imports the same module) and the tests that import types or functions from `../../src/lib/api`.
- **Route audit.** `test/unit/route-audit.test.ts` scans `src/lib/api.ts`, `src/lib/http.ts` and every `src/areas/*/api.ts` (it checks it found ten files), keeps the more-than-20 guard over the union, and compares the union with the fixture. Each of the 77 paths still has a serving file.
- **Build.** `npm run build` before and after, with the hash stripped from each name in `dist/assets` (`sed -E 's/-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8}\.(js|mjs|css|woff2?|png|svg|jpg|webp)$/.\1/'`): the same 115 names. Vite transforms 2413 modules instead of 2404 (the nine new files). Unlike step 17 the hashes are not all the same: 46 names change their hash (the main chunk `index`, the shared chunks `label`, `viewOnly` and one `dist` chunk, and 42 page and component chunks that import the main chunk), because the main chunk's module order changed; every file is the same size to within 0.01 kB (the main chunk is 504.75 kB before and after). The build output is otherwise the same, line for line: no circular-import warning before or after, only the existing notice about chunks over 500 kB. The area modules all land in the main chunk with the barrel, as `api.ts` did (a path from each area module, such as `/api/scan` or `/api/board/my-seats`, is found in `index` and in no other file), so no new shared chunk appears.
- **Merge order.** Ordering rule 3 covers `src/lib/api.ts` and the new modules as well: a branch that adds a call to `src/lib/api.ts` while checkpoint C is open conflicts with the barrel; add it to the area's `api.ts` instead.

- **The boundary rules,** in `eslint.config.js`, written like the `domain/` block (`no-restricted-imports` with `patterns`, a message per pattern):

The rule is carried by `@typescript-eslint/no-restricted-imports`, the same rule with the same options, so it can warn on files where rule 1 is an error (see Deviations).
  3. **Pages do not call fetch (warning).** For `src/pages/**`, `no-restricted-globals` flags `fetch`, and `no-restricted-properties` flags `window.fetch`, `globalThis.fetch` and `self.fetch`. A method called `fetch` on another object, or a function such as `fetchTournaments`, is not flagged.
  The fixtures sit in `test/unit/fixtures/lint`, which the default lint run already skips for the `domain/` fixture.

The second step of checkpoint D. It adds the token layer every later design step builds on, all behind `newLook`: with the switch off the site draws exactly what it drew before, and `test/a11y/baseline.json` is unchanged. The base was `27824cf` (step 20); nothing is committed yet.

  - Packages: `@fontsource-variable/geist-mono` 5.3.0 and `@fontsource/instrument-serif` 5.3.0, both published Sunday, July 19, 2026, exact-pinned, with `package-lock.json` updated by `npm install`.
  - `src/index.css`, `src/main.tsx`, `vite.config.ts`, `src/components/ui/button.tsx`, `src/components/layout/Footer.tsx`, and comments in `src/components/ui/badge.tsx`, `src/lib/brand.ts` and `src/lib/features.ts`. New: `src/lib/colorScheme.ts`, `src/hooks/useColorScheme.ts`, `src/components/AppearanceControl.tsx`.
  - Tests: `test/unit/tokens.test.ts` (25), `test/unit/contrast.test.ts` (150), `test/unit/prepaint-gate.test.ts` (31), `test/unit/token-utilities.test.ts` (25), `test/unit/tokens-scopes.test.ts` (9), `test/unit/geist-mono-glyphs.test.ts` (4), `test/unit/appearance-control.test.tsx` (8), `test/unit/appearance-control-off.test.tsx` (4), `test/unit/redesign-status-step21.test.ts` (11), the shared stylesheet reader `test/unit/helpers/cssTokens.ts`, and `test/a11y/tokens.spec.ts` (18 tests that run on both builds; each skips on the build it does not check).
  - `index.html` is unchanged: its two `theme-color` metas already give `#1a2744` for light and `#0b1220` for dark.
- **Today's values on the plain `:root`.** The semantic tokens are `--ground`, `--surface`, `--surface-2`, `--raised`, `--ink`, `--ink-muted`, `--hairline`, `--field` (the field border), `--ok`, `--bad`, `--gold`, `--gold-ink`, `--gold-on-dark`, `--focus` and `--font-mono-face`, plus a text colour and a tint for each status (open, soon, full, waitlist, closed, live, partner, lca). The plain `:root` gives each one the value the site shows today: `--ground` is the stock `--background`, `--ink` is navy `#1a2744`, `--surface` is `#fff`, `--gold-ink` is `#c8a94a`, the statuses are the light tones `StatusBadge` draws, `--focus` is `color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring) 50%, transparent)`, which is the very value Tailwind compiles `ring-ring/50` to, and `--font-mono-face` is Tailwind's own monospace stack. The plain `:root` block stays first and the stock `.dark` block stays after it, untouched, so the baseline checks in `browser-test-wiring.test.ts` read the same values.
- **The new look.** Every new rule starts with `:root[data-look="new"]`, which `src/main.tsx` sets on `<html>` when `newLook` is on. Base is Looks-3 Minimal (navy ink, `#fff` and `#f7f8fa` surfaces, `#e5e7ed` borders, `#5b6478` muted, ok `#047857`, bad `#c0362c`, gold `#c8a94a` as a fill, gold-ink `#866a1e`, `--font-mono-face` `'Geist Mono Variable'` and then the system stack). `.dark` under the new look is the Looks-3 dark palette (`#0b1220`, `#111a2c`, `#1a2744`, ink `#e8ecf4`, muted `#9aa6bf`). `[data-theme="live"]`, `[data-theme="scholastic"]` and `[data-theme="heritage"]` carry the Looks-7, Looks-6 and Looks-1 tile values (heritage `--gold-ink` `#705718`; heritage under `.dark` keeps the Minimal dark grounds), and `[data-theme=""]` puts the base look back, light or dark. The shadcn variables (`--background`, `--foreground`, `--card`, `--muted-foreground`, `--border`, `--input`, `--ring` and the rest) point at the tokens only under the new look, on `<html>` and on every scope, so a component inside a scope takes that scope's colours and the stock `.dark` greys never show. `@theme inline` adds the utilities (`text-ink`, `text-ink-muted`, `bg-ground`, `bg-surface`, `bg-surface-2`, `bg-raised`, `border-hairline`, `border-field`, `bg-gold`, `text-gold-ink`, `text-gold-on-dark`, `text-ok`, `text-bad`, `ring-focus`, `text-status-open`, `bg-status-open-tint` and so on) and `--font-mono: var(--font-mono-face)`. The dark variant is `(&:where(.dark, .dark *))`.
- **Focus.** The Button's glow reads `ring-focus`, which with `newLook` off is today's half-strength ring, measured the same before and after (`oklab(0.708 0 0 / 0.5) 0px 0px 0px 3px`, border `oklch(0.708 0 0)`, no outline). Under the new look one rule outside the layers gives every `:focus-visible` element a 2px solid `--focus` outline with a 2px gap and turns off the shadcn glow while it shows, so a control draws one ring: navy on light grounds, gold on dark and live grounds, and gold inside a `bg-lca-navy` band (today's header, footer and the `PageHero` bands) or inside any element marked `data-ground="dark"`. The homepage hero is not a navy band: its navy is a tint laid over the photo beside the buttons, not around them, so until a later step marks it, its buttons, arrows and dots get the navy ring on a dark photo (about 1.2:1). The red and blue announcement banners are in the same position. Both are under Follow-ups, and `newLook` stays off until they are fixed.
- **Motion.** Under the new look, `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` sets every animation and transition to 0 seconds with no delay and one iteration. A zero-length animation still ends, so the dialogs that wait for their closing animation still close.
- **Fonts.** Geist Mono is imported once and named only in the new look's `--font-mono-face`, so with `newLook` off no page asks for it (the browser test watches the network on the finished event's page) and the eighteen `font-mono` uses keep the device's font. Instrument Serif 400 is `font-accent`; nothing uses it yet, and a font file is fetched only when a page uses it.
- **Appearance.** `src/lib/colorScheme.ts` holds System, Light and Dark, the `lca-appearance` key in `localStorage` (every read and write in `try`/`catch`; System removes the key), and `PREPAINT_SCRIPT`, a one-line ES5 script that sets `data-look="new"` and `.dark` before the first paint. `vite.config.ts` writes that script at the top of the page head only when the build has `newLook` on; it reads the switch from the text of `src/lib/features.ts` and, in the `a11y` mode only, from `VITE_FLAGS`, the same rule as `applyFlagOverrides`, because the config cannot import a file that reads `import.meta.env`. A build without the switch carries no script, so nothing can add `.dark` and wake the stock dark block. `src/hooks/useColorScheme.ts` applies a choice and follows the device setting as it changes, and adds `.dark` only when `newLook` is on. `AppearanceControl` (three buttons with `aria-pressed`, labelled "Appearance") sits in the current footer's bottom line under `newLook`; with the switch off the footer keeps its empty line.
- **The switches keep their own chunk.** `src/main.tsx` now imports `FEATURES`, which would fold the switches into the entry chunk; `builds.spec.ts` loads `features-[hash].js` to prove which build a port serves. A `codeSplitting` group in `vite.config.ts` keeps that file; the build's other 104 scripts are the same list as before.

### Step 22: ThemeScope, the route-to-look map and the live fonts

The third step of checkpoint D. It adds the mechanism every themed area will use, and nothing renders it outside the browser-test fixture page, so the site draws exactly what it drew before and `test/a11y/baseline.json` is unchanged. The base was `aaa001b`; nothing is committed yet.

- **Files.**
  - Packages: `@fontsource/barlow` and `@fontsource/barlow-condensed` 5.3.0, both published Sunday, July 19, 2026, exact-pinned, with `package-lock.json` updated by `npm install --save-exact`.
  - New: `src/components/ThemeScope.tsx`, `src/lib/themeScopes.ts`, `src/styles/themes/live.css` (the `src/styles` folder is new). Changed: `src/pages/fixtures/ScopeFixturePage.tsx`.
  - Tests: `test/unit/themeScopes.test.ts` (18), `test/unit/theme-scope.test.tsx` (31), `test/unit/theme-scope-edges.test.tsx` (12), `test/unit/theme-scope-wiring.test.ts` (20), `test/unit/themeScopes-edges.test.ts` (14), `test/a11y/scope-switch.spec.ts` (4 tests on both builds) and `test/a11y/scope-switch-edges.spec.ts` (6 tests on both builds).
- **ThemeScope.** It takes `scope` (`base`, `heritage`, `live` or `scholastic`) and writes `data-theme` on a wrapper, `""` for base, which puts the base look back. The wrapper is `display: contents` so layout does not change; `layout="box"` keeps a real box (the fixture container needs one, because `tokens.spec.ts` reads its background), and `as` is `div`, `main` or `section`. Ordinary HTML attributes pass through, but a `data-theme` among them cannot override the scope. The token blocks are already in `src/index.css` from step 21, so a switch never shows base colours for a moment.
- **Nesting.** One level only. Base inside heritage is the one nesting allowed (editors and forms on a heritage page stay base); heritage inside live, every other pair and two levels deep are reported with `console.warn`, once per change. The rule lives in `nestingProblem` in `src/lib/themeScopes.ts`, because `react-refresh` objects to a component file that exports other things. The check runs in every mode except the production build.
- **routeScope(pathname).** It ignores case, a trailing slash, a query and a hash, as React Router does. The admin, workspace, manage, dashboard, account and board inbox prefixes are checked first and are always base; the six heritage pages (`/about`, `/governance/board`, `/governance/bylaws`, `/governance/minutes`, `/meeting`, `/champions`) resolve to heritage; everything else, the three redirect addresses included, is base. It returns only base or heritage: the live look follows event state and scholastic waits for WS11.
- **Fonts.** A scope's font CSS is imported lazily the first time that scope renders, and an import that fails is retried by the next one. Only live has a loader today; heritage arrives in step 30 and scholastic in WS11. `live.css` holds only `@import` lines: Barlow Condensed 500, 600, 700 and 800 and Barlow 400, 500 and 600, the weights the Looks-7 tile names. It binds no `font-family` yet, so no font file downloads; the production build carries no ThemeScope, no `live-*.css` and no Barlow files.
- **The fixture page.** Its container renders through `ThemeScope` with `layout="box"`. The scholastic fixture gains the grade-band tiles built from the `--*-tile` and hue tokens: K-3 Coral, K-5 Mint, K-8 Sky, K-12 Grape and a Gold tile marked "Tiles", the board's word for it, in the board's dark gold `#705718` read from `--status-soon` (the en dash is written as an escape because `browser-test-wiring.test.ts` bans dash characters in that file). Its header comment is rewritten. No control was added: the switch in AC8 is made by the test.
- Checks: `npm run lint` is 34 errors and 13 warnings before and after, none in a touched file. `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck:functions` and `npm run check:bundle` pass (no zod in 125 files). `npm run test:all` passes: unit 2236 tests in 94 files (2141 in 89 before; 95 added in the five new files), integration 790 in 58 (unchanged). In the first full run `test/unit/drizzle-baseline.test.ts` timed out twice at 5000 ms while Playwright and wrangler ran at the same time; that file alone passed 26 of 26 and the later full run passed. `npm run test:a11y`, with `PW_CHROMIUM_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium`: 111 passed and 18 skipped in 1.8 minutes (91 and 18 before; 20 added: the two new specs on both builds); the baseline comparison matched and `test/a11y/baseline.json` is unmodified. The `Network connection lost` lines in the log come from the `/api/me` role-safety case in `seeded-data.spec.ts`, which calls the fake Supabase on a closed port. `scanner:check` was not run; nothing under `scanner/` or `functions/utils/scan/` changed.
