It rewrites classes in string literals and in the text of template literals, and in the quoted strings of commented-out code. In a comment it takes whatever lies between two matching quote marks on one line as a quoted string, so a line of prose with two apostrophes in it counts as one too, and a watched class between them would be rewritten, though the script's header says prose never is. The seven comment rewrites in this tree are all commented-out code (see Follow-ups). The map lists the classes it watches (`text-lca-navy`, `bg-white`, `bg-lca-navy`), six rules tried in order, three sites (one string in one file, where the rule would be wrong) and six keep entries, each with a reason. A rewrite keeps the class's variants (`hover:`, `md:`, `[&_a]:`), its opacity modifier and its `!` mark. It stops before writing anything on a watched class with no rule or keep entry, a class that runs into a `${}` substitution, a string with an escape, a site or keep entry that does not name exactly one string, or a keep entry that matches nothing. `--dry-run` prints the plan; `--check` fails when anything is left to rewrite, which is how the unit test holds the tree to the map. The run rewrote 487 classes in 75 files and kept 39; a second run rewrites none. ### Step 25: gold text off light grounds

The sixth step of checkpoint D. Brand gold `#c8a94a` reads 2.28:1 on white, so the brief keeps it as text on navy only, where it reads 6.51:1. Every `text-lca-gold` on a light ground now takes the gold-ink token, and the gold the pages spelled as hex colours takes three gold tokens of its own, so under the new look no gold text sits on a light ground at 2.28:1. With `newLook` off every class paints the colour it replaced, so nothing visible changes and `test/a11y/baseline.json` is unchanged. A guard keeps gold text off light grounds from here on. The base was `3d80a0e` (step 24); nothing is committed yet.

- **The script.** `scripts/codemods/gold-ink.ts` reads every TSX file under `src` with the parser of `scripts/codemods/semantic-colours.ts` and finds the element each `text-lca-gold` sits on: the one whose className holds the string, directly or through a constant of the same file. From there up through the ancestors the first ground decides: navy for an opaque `bg-brand-navy` or `bg-lca-navy`, an inline navy, a hex ground on which brand gold reads 4.5:1 or anything passed to `PageHero`, `Navbar` or `Footer`; light for any other opaque ground (a hex one only where the light look's dark gold reads 4.5:1), a Card, an outline Button or what a dialog draws, unless the Card's or the dialog's className gives a ground of its own, which is read first. A tint lets the walk go on (an inline one too: a club colour's tint, an rgba below 1, or a colour given two hex digits of alpha, as the admin's colour preview draws it), a hover ground is not the resting ground, and a ground in a className counts only where its `?:` branch or `&&` guard also holds for the gold (the admin sidebar's icon is gold only in the branch where its link is navy). A component of the site among the ancestors is read inside, for the ground it paints where what it is given lands: around its `{children}` or the prop the gold is passed in, or, for a gold class given as its className, at the element that takes it; the caller's own classes land on each of its elements that takes the className or spreads the props. At the top of a component the walk follows the component to every place it is drawn, in its own file or in a file that imports it under any name (renamed, a default, a namespace or `lazy()`), `forwardRef()` and `memo()` included, but never a component of the same name from another module or a package. That is how the More menu's button, `NavLinkItem` and `DrawerLink` in `Navbar.tsx` are placed on the navy header, the scanner's panel is read as the card it paints, and each page is followed to its route in `src/App.tsx`. Anything it cannot settle (a string no className reads, a ground that may or may not apply, a ground it does not know, a component drawn on both kinds of ground or drawing what it is given on both) is a person's decision and an entry of `test/unit/fixtures/goldAllowlist.ts`; an entry for a use it can place is refused. It prints a review table of every use, with its ground, what decided it, what the run does and the element it sits on, and writes it to the file `--table` names (the scratchpad, not the repository). `data-ground="dark"`, the focus ring's marker, is not a colour: beside a navy of its own (the club heroes' inline navy) the navy decides, and on the home page hero, the one element marked with it and no navy, a darkened photo, the script cannot tell what brand gold reads, so a use there is unplaced, as on a hex ground where neither gold reads 4.5:1 (see Judgement calls). `--check` fails on any `text-lca-gold` left on a light ground, any `text-gold-ink` on navy or on a ground it cannot place, and any allowlist count that is wrong.

### Step 26: status tags, the gold button, filter chips, date blocks and the scroll panel

The seventh step of checkpoint D. It builds the base components the later workstreams assemble pages from. StatusBadge gains a status prop that shows each of eight statuses in words, as the Looks-3 tile's tag on the status tokens, and its tone and on props keep drawing today's pills class for class; StatusDot says its state in words under the new look; the shared Button gains a gold variant; and `FilterChip`, `DateBlock` and `ScrollPanel` are new. The new components are drawn only on the fixture page, which exists only in the accessibility test build, and no page file changes; the one existing part whose output changes is StatusDot, whose words appear in the `/tournaments` list with `newLook` on. With `newLook` off nothing a visitor sees changes, so `test/a11y/baseline.json` is unchanged. The base was `a74f221` (step 25); nothing is committed yet.

  - The status path draws the tile's tag (`.t-tag` on the Looks-3 Minimal tile): 24px high, a 6px radius, 12px words in weight 500 and a 6px gap, the same box in every look. Its words are its children, or, when it has none or they draw nothing (nothing at all, a boolean, blank text, or a list or a fragment holding only those, as `drawsNothing` in `src/lib/drawsNothing.ts` tells them), its status's default words; an element of any other kind is taken as words, since what it draws is known only when it renders. The tag carries `data-status` and `data-slot="status-badge"`.

- **ScrollPanel** (`src/components/ScrollPanel.tsx`). From K's October 8 note: `ADMIN_SCROLL` made a component, a box bounded by the viewport (70vh, which a `max-h-*` in its className replaces) that scrolls on its own with its overscroll kept inside, framed by a hairline on the surface, with an optional header held at its top on a ground of its own; a header that draws nothing (false, blank text or an empty fragment, as `header={cond && ...}` gives when its condition fails) adds no header bar. It is a region named by its `label`, in the tab order (`tabIndex` 0), so Tab reaches it and the arrow, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End keys scroll it. Its header is drawn over the top of the scrolling box, so a browser takes a control under it for one already in view and leaves it hidden there when the keyboard moves to it, as Shift+Tab does after a person scrolls a form down (WCAG 2.4.11, Focus Not Obscured). The panel's scroll padding is therefore the header's height and the focus ring's 4px reach (the new look's 2px gap and 2px line, which also covers today's 3px glow), read as the header is drawn and again, through a `ResizeObserver`, whenever its height changes, so the browser scrolls such a control out from under the header, ring and all; with no header there is no padding. No page uses it yet (see Follow-ups).

### Step 27: chess data, result cells and the table primitives

The eighth step of checkpoint D. Chess data reads as the brief asks under the new look: scores and tiebreaks are written with ½ by `formatScore`, their figures are in the monospace face with tabular figures, each round of a crosstable shows its result by its letter, by a drawn mark for the colour played and in words, and the two tables' headers are real header cells, the player's name heading each row. The table primitives gain what that needs, each opt-in: `TableHead` says `scope="col"`, `TableRowHeader` is new, `stickyFirst` pins the first column or the first two on the opaque surface, `label` makes the table's box a named region in the tab order and `bounded` bounds it with its header held at the top. With `newLook` off both tables draw today's markup with `scope="col"` added to their header cells, which draws nothing new, so nothing a visitor sees changes and `test/a11y/baseline.json` is unchanged. The base was `a12c74e` (step 26); nothing is committed yet.

The result cell of the Live-C board (`.rc`): 24px high, a 6px radius, at least 58px wide, a 4px gap and 13px figures in the monospace face at weight 500, holding the result's letter, the mark of the colour the player had and the opponent's number, as "W ○ 17". The letter, the mark and the number are hidden from screen readers, and the cell's words, in a visually hidden span, say the game: "Won with White against 17", "Lost by forfeit against 7", "Full-point bye", "Half-point bye", "Did not play", "No result yet, with Black against 4"; an `aria-label` on a span with no role is not allowed in ARIA 1.2. A mark shows only where a colour was played: a win, a loss, a draw and a game with no result yet. On paper the cell gives up its height and its 58px width and may wrap. `ResultLegend`, the key, says that each game shows the result, the color played and the opponent's number, then gives each letter with its words and the two marks with the words White and Black.
- **The table primitives** (`src/components/ui/table.tsx`). Each new prop is opt-in: a table drawn as the fixture page drew it gets today's markup to the letter but for `scope="col"` on its header cells, and its box keeps its three classes and gains no attribute.
  - `TableHead` writes `scope="col"` unless given another scope, which draws nothing new; `TableRowHeader` is a `th` with `scope="row"`, spaced like a cell, in weight 500.
  - `stickyFirst` pins the first column (`true`) or the first two (`2`) to the left edge while the table scrolls sideways. The table then draws its row lines on the cells (`border-separate`), so a line moves with a pinned cell rather than staying where a collapsed table draws it, and each pinned cell paints the opaque surface (`bg-surface`: `#fff` in the light looks, `#111a2c` in dark mode, `#0e1526` in the live look, `#fffdf8` in heritage) with its row's tint laid over it as an image. A row's tint is a custom property, `--row-tint`, which the row paints as well, so a pinned cell always matches its row: today's header tint and first place's gold tint are set that way, the hover tint and a selected row's tint by the table itself, and the rows do not fade, so a row and its pinned cells change together. The second column sticks at the first's width, read from the first cell as the table is drawn and again through a `ResizeObserver` when it changes, since a shared place such as 12-15 widens its column; a line down the last pinned column's right edge, in the border colour of the look the table sits in, marks where the rest scrolls under it.
  - `label` makes the box the table scrolls in a region named by it, in the tab order with the focus ring, as `ScrollPanel` is, so the keyboard can scroll a table wider than a phone. `bounded`, which the types allow only with a label, bounds the box by the viewport (70vh, which a `max-h-*` in `containerClassName` replaces) with its overscroll kept inside, and holds the header row at the top on the surface, its corner above the pinned columns. Both keep a control the keyboard moves to clear of what is pinned, with a scroll padding of the pinned header's height and the pinned columns' width plus the focus ring's 4px reach, measured as `ScrollPanel` measures its header (WCAG 2.4.11). On paper every cell is static, the pinned cells and a bounded box's header with them, and a bounded box prints whole; the print rule is written important, since the selectors that pin a cell or the header are more specific than it.
  - `containerClassName` carries the box's classes, which today's tables put on a scroll wrapper of their own. The file imports neither `ScrollPanel` nor `ADMIN_SCROLL`, whose importers `test/unit/base-components-scope.test.ts` pins; the bound is written in the file.

### Step 29: the still hero picture and nothing that moves on by itself

The tenth step of checkpoint D. Under `newLook` the homepage hero no longer moves on by itself: it is one still picture of slide 1, under the darkening, tint, gradient and label its slide had, with today's words, buttons and figures, and `HeroSlideshow`, whose timer moved the slides on every 5 seconds, is not drawn, so the page sets no timer. The picture comes from the image pipeline the step builds: `scripts/images.mjs`, run by hand with sharp, writes each slide photo as AVIF and WebP at 640, 1024 and 1600 pixels into `src/assets/generated`, 30 committed files of 200,000 bytes or less, so a build never needs sharp, and `ResponsiveImage` draws one as a `<picture>` from which the browser takes the smallest file the screen needs. A test reads every timer in `src`, and `npm run perf:home` measures `/` in the lab. With `newLook` off `HomePage.tsx` draws today's slideshow to the attribute, so `test/a11y/baseline.json` is unchanged. Nothing under `public/`, `functions/`, `workers/` or `index.html` changes, `src/assets/hero.png` is left as it is and out of the pipeline, and nothing is added to `test/a11y/known-violations.json`. - **ResponsiveImage** (`src/components/ResponsiveImage.tsx`). A picture in the sizes and formats the image script writes: a `<picture>` with an AVIF source and a WebP source, each listing its files by width (`srcset`) with the `sizes` the caller gives, so the browser takes, in the first format it can show, the smallest file that covers the space the picture fills at the screen's density. The img inside carries the source photo's own width and height, so the page holds the picture's shape before a file arrives and nothing moves when one does. The page's largest picture, the one a visitor sees first, is marked `priority`: it is fetched ahead of other pictures (`fetchpriority="high"`) and loaded at once (`loading="eager"`); every other picture waits until it nears the screen (`loading="lazy"`). The caller imports the files it draws one by one, so a build carries only the files its pages use, and must also give the img's own `src` (`fallback`): the photo in a format every browser shows, taken only by a browser that can show neither AVIF nor WebP (an older Safari, for one) and never fetched by one that takes a source. The hero gives slide 1's own JPEG, the file the slideshow draws. It takes the picture's words (`alt`, empty for decoration), a class and a style, which the hero uses for its darkening. The file exports the component and its props type only, for the only-export-components rule; its type for one file is not exported.
- **The image script** (`scripts/images.mjs`, `npm run images`). Run by hand with sharp 0.34.5, never by a build or a test: it writes each of `LCA_Slide_1.jpg` to `LCA_Slide_5.jpg` (2048 pixels wide, 2,171,020 bytes in all) as AVIF and as WebP at 640, 1024 and 1600 pixels wide into `src/assets/generated`, named `LCA_Slide_<n>-<width>.avif` and `.webp`, each at its photo's own shape. `src/assets/hero.png` is left out, because no page or file uses it. Each file must be 200,000 bytes or less, which holds either reading of the brief's 200 KB; the script checks every file it writes and stops with an error, once it has written them all, when one is over. Its quality table: AVIF at 60 and WebP at 75 for every file but four, slide 3 at 1600 pixels as AVIF at 55 (195,594 bytes) and WebP at 48 (192,900 bytes), and slide 5 at 1600 pixels as AVIF at 57 (188,139 bytes) and WebP at 60 (191,364 bytes); at the usual qualities those four are 228,891, 264,114, 210,463 and 229,892 bytes. The largest of the others is slide 1's 1600 pixel WebP, 175,804 bytes, and the file a 390 pixel phone at three times density takes for the hero, slide 1's 1600 pixel AVIF, is 162,969. Both formats are written at effort 4, the AVIF with its colour at half resolution (4:2:0), as the photos' own JPEG files and every lossy WebP store it, where sharp's default for AVIF is full resolution; at the same quality that makes each AVIF file 6 to 11 per cent smaller. Nothing is copied from the photos but their pixels: no camera data and no colour profile. Slides 2, 3 and 5 carry a Display P3 profile, which sharp uses to turn their colours into sRGB, the colour space of every file written. Two runs wrote the same 30 files byte for byte, in 51 seconds each.

- **The timer test.** `test/unit/no-rotation.test.ts` reads every `.ts` and `.tsx` file under `src` (not TSX alone: the price clock is a hook in a `.ts` file) with the TypeScript parser, so it counts calls, not a type such as `ReturnType<typeof setInterval>` or a word in a comment. Every `setInterval`, bare or called on `window`, `globalThis` or `self`, must be named in its allowlist by its file, with its reason and its number of calls, which must match, so a new one fails and a removed one must take its entry down. There are four entries and five calls: HomePage, two (the slideshow with `newLook` off, both inside `HeroSlideshow`, which the test checks is drawn only then, listed until WS03 deletes it), AdminEmailPage, one (the list of campaigns read again every 3 seconds while one is sending), AnnualMeetingPage, one (the countdown's clock, once a minute) and useNow, one (the price clock in `src/hooks/useNow.ts`, every 30 seconds). A `setTimeout` or `requestAnimationFrame` that runs again by itself fails wherever it is: one whose callback is, or calls, the function it sits in, and one in an effect that runs again once its callback sets a state. An effect runs again on a state its dependency list names, or on one a value in the list is read from (`const slide = slides[index]`, through `useMemo` or not, followed through the component's own values as far as they go); an effect with no dependency list, with a list that is not written out, or with a list naming a function, object or list written in the component without a hook to keep it (made anew on every render) runs after every render, so any state its timer sets makes a loop. The callback is followed through the functions the file defines, so a helper between them changes nothing, and a function given to `useCallback`, or written as a class method or field, goes by its name. What the test does not read is a timer that runs again only by way of another file, a prop or a context, or through a class component's lifecycle methods; those are for review. The seven one-shot timers in the tree (a debounce, a reload, a give-up, a scroll, a copied message, a map listener's removal and a released download address) pass. It fails on each case planted in a temporary tree, the timers' names put together when the test runs: a `setInterval` in a TSX page, one in a `.ts` hook called on `window`, a timer that schedules itself, one whose callback calls the function it sits in, a frame that asks for the next, a slideshow on an effect that lists its state, a carousel whose effect runs a helper on the timer or hands it a reducer's dispatch, a timer that a `useCallback`, a class method or a class field schedules again, two functions that call each other through the timer, an effect with no dependency list and one with a list that is not written out, an effect that lists a value read from the state (directly and through `useMemo`), an effect that lists a function made anew on every render (an arrow function and a function declaration), a third call in `HomePage.tsx`, and an entry left up after its calls are gone. It passes the one-shot cases planted beside them: a debounce whose helper sets only what its effect does not depend on, a message a helper clears once, an effect with an empty list, one whose list names only a prop, one that names a function kept by `useCallback`, and one that names a figure read from an object made in the component.
- **The lab check** (`scripts/perf-home.ts`, `npm run perf:home`). Run with `node --no-warnings --experimental-strip-types`, like `scripts/check-bundle.ts`; ESLint reads it with the TypeScript rules, and no compiler project includes it. It builds `dist-a11y-on` and the seeded local database as `npm run test:a11y` does, through `buildVariant` and `buildDatabase` from `test/a11y/global-setup.ts`, whose import runs nothing (local only, never a remote database), serves the build with `wrangler pages dev` on 127.0.0.1:8801 with the same fake settings and empty secrets (`a11yServerArgs`), starts Chromium headless with a debugging port, runs Lighthouse 13.5.0 on `/` through it, three times unless told, and stops both. Before it builds anything it checks that nothing listens on a port the test servers use (8801 and 8802, and their inspector ports 9231 and 9232), and stops if something does, so it measures only a server it started, as `playwright.config.ts` does with `reuseExistingServer: false`, and does not make the build and the database again under a server that is serving them; it checks the server's two ports once more just before starting it, and counts an answer from `/` only while that server runs. The server and the browser run in process groups of their own, so it stops them itself: when it ends, when the browser has not opened its debugging port after 30 seconds, and when it is stopped by Ctrl-C, by SIGTERM (which `timeout` sends and npm passes on) or by SIGHUP, asking each to stop and killing what still runs 10 seconds later. A server answering on 8801 and a listener on 9232, each planted before a run, stopped it within a second, before any build; SIGTERM, SIGHUP and SIGINT sent in the middle of a run, and a stand-in browser that never opened its port, each left no process, port or profile folder behind. For each run it prints the performance score, the five metrics, the LCP element with its time and how that breaks down, the pictures and the largest files fetched, and the insights that found something with what they name; then the scores and their median. The score is a measurement written down here, not a gate, and the script never fails on one. The browser is the one the browser tests use, `PW_CHROMIUM_PATH` when it is set and otherwise Playwright's own Chromium, started by the script with the settings Lighthouse's own launcher gives it (and without its sandbox when run by root, as in a container) rather than through chrome-launcher, so the check needs no package beyond lighthouse; and it refuses every host but 127.0.0.1, as the accessibility tests do, so neither the browser's own calls home nor anything outside enters the measurement. Its header says never to run it beside `npm run test:a11y` or beside itself, since they share the port, the build folder and the database folder. `--reuse` serves the build and the database as they are, `--runs` sets the number of runs and `--out` keeps each run's full report.

### Step 30: the heritage look's type, loaded only inside its scope

The eleventh step of checkpoint D. It adds the Heritage Club look's type: `src/styles/themes/heritage.css`, which `ThemeScope` imports lazily the first time a heritage scope renders, holds the latin files of Libre Caslon Display and Source Serif 4, a Georgia fallback face for each, the `--font-display` and `--font-text` tokens, the type rules a heritage page opts into on its own elements (display headings and figures, a document's reading column, the 2px radius of cards, tables and mats, and small capitals), and the base look's accent face switched off. Every rule that sets a face, a size, a radius or a measure waits for `newLook`, as the heritage colours do. Nothing draws a heritage scope but the fixture page, which exists only in the browser-test build and carries none of the hooks, so the site draws what it drew before: the production build is the same, byte for byte, and `test/a11y/baseline.json` is unchanged. Nothing under `public/`, `functions/`, `workers/`, `src/pages`, `src/components/ui` or `index.html` changes, and `src/index.css`, on the step's list, is not changed. The base was `abe7d07`, the commit after step 29 that gave each browser-test server a database of its own; nothing is committed yet.

The average width is Capsize's, each character's advance weighted by how often it occurs in English text: recomputed from the 5.3.0 files with the weights of `@capsizecss/unpack` 4.0.1, it is 374 for Caslon, 479 for Source Serif 4 and 441 for its italic, the numbers Capsize publishes. So size-adjust is (face width / 1000) / (Georgia width / 2048), and each override the face's metric over its 1000 units, divided by size-adjust: Caslon 83.89%, ascent 115.62%, descent 31.71% and line gap 0%; Source Serif 107.45%, 96.42%, 31.18% and 0%; its italic 97.01%, 106.79%, 34.53% and 0%. ### Step 31: the heritage layout on its six pages

The twelfth step of checkpoint D. With `themeHeritage` on, the six heritage pages (About, Board, Bylaws, Minutes, Annual meeting and Champions) are drawn in the Heritage Club look: `src/App.tsx` puts their routes inside `HeritageLayout`, a lazy layout route that draws them in a heritage scope on the look's paper ground, under `newLook` holds each page until the look's stylesheet has arrived, for three seconds at most, and tells the parts inside it to put on the look's hooks and, under `newLook`, its thick-thin rules and seal; the governance documents' add and edit card, with its editor, and an admin's forms on the Board page are reset to the base look; and heritage's controls take the base look's tokens, so a Button, a field, a status tag and the focus ring are the same pixels in either look. With `themeHeritage` off the six routes are listed as before and each page draws its markup to the attribute, so `test/a11y/baseline.json` is unchanged; with `themeHeritage` on and `newLook` off the pages are wrapped but look as they do today. The production build now carries the layout, `ThemeScope` and both looks' stylesheets and font files; no page fetches a look's stylesheet or its faces until it draws that look, while the step's new chunks of code are fetched by the pages that import them whatever the switches say (see Build). No package is added, nothing under `public/`, `functions/`, `workers/`, `migrations/` or `index.html` changes, and `src/lib/themeScopes.ts` and `src/styles/themes/heritage.css` are not changed. The base was `0cc7c30` (step 30); nothing is committed yet.

- **Files.**
  - New: `src/layouts/HeritageLayout.tsx` (the `src/layouts` folder is new), `src/contexts/heritage-layout.ts` (the context the layout provides and its three readers), `src/lib/scopeStylesheets.ts` (the looks' stylesheet loader), `src/components/ThickThinRule.tsx` and `src/components/Seal.tsx`, each exporting its component and its props type only; `test/unit/governanceEditors.test.tsx` (5), `test/unit/heritage-layout.test.tsx` (53), `test/unit/heritage-ornaments.test.tsx` (9), `test/unit/scope-stylesheets.test.tsx` (16), their helpers `test/unit/helpers/heritagePages.tsx` (the six pages drawn on their own) and `test/unit/helpers/heritageAnswers.ts` (made-up answers for their requests), the fixture `test/unit/fixtures/heritage-pages-today.ts` (the six pages' markup at `0cc7c30`, by length and sha256), `test/unit/redesign-status-step31.test.ts` (33: these records), `test/unit/heritage-controls-tokens.test.tsx` (43: the controls' colours inside heritage and base worked out from `src/index.css`, light, dark and printed, and the controls rule held to the base look), `test/unit/heritage-app-routes.test.tsx` (28: `src/App.tsx` drawn whole with the switch on and off), `test/unit/heritage-hooks.test.tsx` (31: the context's readers, `PageHero` and `GovLayout` inside and outside the layout, and the fixture page's heritage parts), `test/unit/scope-stylesheets-edges.test.tsx` (4: the loader with two stylesheets, an address with a query or a fragment, and a failed link taken out of the page), `test/unit/governanceEditors-bylaws.test.tsx` (3: the Bylaws page's three lists for an admin) and `test/unit/governanceEditors-board.test.tsx` (4: the Board page's forms for an admin), and `test/a11y/heritage.spec.ts` (45 tests on each build; 45 run on `a11y-on` and 21 on `a11y-off`, each skipping on the build it does not check).
  - Changed: `src/App.tsx`, `src/components/ThemeScope.tsx`, `src/components/PageHero.tsx`, `src/areas/governance/components/GovLayout.tsx`, `src/areas/governance/components/GovernanceDocuments.tsx`, the six pages (`src/pages/AboutPage.tsx`, `src/pages/BoardPage.tsx`, `src/pages/BylawsPage.tsx`, `src/pages/MinutesPage.tsx`, `src/pages/AnnualMeetingPage.tsx` and `src/pages/ChampionsPage.tsx`), `src/pages/fixtures/ScopeFixturePage.tsx` (the heritage fixture only), `src/index.css` (one rule, for heritage's controls) and `docs/redesign/REDESIGN_SPEC.md` (the step's sentence in the WS01 deviations list).
  - Tests changed: `test/unit/themeScopes.test.ts` (24, 21 before), `test/unit/theme-scope-wiring.test.ts` (37, 21 before), `test/unit/theme-scope.test.tsx` (33, as before), `test/unit/theme-scope-edges.test.tsx` (15, as before), `test/unit/app-routes.test.tsx` (36, 35 before), `test/unit/heritage-edges.test.ts` (29, 28 before), `test/unit/heritage-scope-edges.test.tsx` (17, as before), `test/unit/lca-mark.test.tsx` (36, as before), `test/unit/brand-edges.test.tsx` (32, as before), `test/unit/goldText.test.ts` (129, as before), `test/unit/tokens.test.ts` (59, as before), `test/unit/browser-test-wiring.test.ts` (93, 92 before), `test/unit/redesign-status-step30.test.ts` (its three acceptance row pins), `test/a11y/brand.spec.ts` and `test/a11y/brand-edges.spec.ts`; what each moves is under Deviations, Step 31.
- **The layout.** `src/layouts/HeritageLayout.tsx` draws `ThemeScope scope="heritage"` as a box (`layout="box"`) on a div marked `data-layout="heritage"`, inside the `<main>` that `src/App.tsx` puts round every route: the spec's table puts `data-theme="heritage"` on `<main>`, but the site's main already holds every route, and a second main landmark is what `ThemeScope`'s header and the step 22 follow-up warn against (see Deviations). The box paints the look's paper ground with `bg-ground`, the ground token itself, and its ink with `text-foreground`, and casts its ground downward as a shadow (`shadow-[0_100vh_0_100vh_var(--ground)]`) that the footer, drawn after it, covers, so on a page shorter than the window the paper runs down to the footer without adding to the page's height or its scrolling. The header and the footer sit outside the box and keep the base look. Inside the box the layout provides the heritage layout context and a Suspense boundary that holds the page (`<Outlet />`) beside `ScopeStylesheetReady`, which it draws under `newLook` only. `GovLayout` stays inside the four pages that draw it (About, Board, Bylaws and Minutes) and `PageHero` inside the other two, which draw it themselves; the layout adds no markup to a page beyond the box, the hooks, the rules and the seal, and `GovLayout`'s column.
- **The routes.** `src/App.tsx` writes the six routes once, each as it was (`<Route path="/about" element={<AboutPage />} />` and the rest), in one constant, `HERITAGE_PAGES`, and, where the `/meeting` and `/about` routes stood, draws that constant inside a layout route with no path of its own, `<Route element={<HeritageLayout />}>`, when `FEATURES.themeHeritage` is on, and on its own when it is off. With the switch off the list of routes is today's: React Router reads a fragment's routes as its own and ranks routes by their paths, not their order. The three redirects (`/governance`, `/state-champions` and `/governance/rules`) stay outside the layout. The layout is loaded with `lazy()` like the pages, and `src/App.tsx` names no `ThemeScope`.
- **The stylesheet before the first paint.** The import of the looks' files moves out of `ThemeScope` into `src/lib/scopeStylesheets.ts`, which only `src/components/ThemeScope.tsx` names: each look's file is asked for once for the whole visit, as one promise that settles when the file has loaded or could not be, and never rejects. A scope still asks for its file in an effect. `ScopeStylesheetReady`, exported beside `ThemeScope`, draws nothing and holds its Suspense boundary until the file has arrived, starting the request itself when no scope has, for three seconds at most (`HOLD_AT_MOST_MS`): what it waits on is one promise per request, made the first time a page waits on it, which settles when the request does or when the three seconds have passed, and after that the loader gives nothing to wait on for that request, so on a slow or stalled connection the page is drawn in the type it has and takes the look's type when the file arrives, as when the file cannot be loaded at all. `HeritageLayout` draws it under `newLook` only, since with `newLook` off none of the file's rules apply and a wait would buy nothing; the scope still asks for the file. It sits after the `<Outlet />`, inside the layout's own boundary, so the page's code and the stylesheet are fetched at once and the page's first paint is in the look's type: on `a11y-on` the page's heading enters the page in the display face at 36 pixels with the stylesheet already in place, and with the stylesheet held back the loading line stays and no h1 is drawn, for three seconds at most; held back longer, the heading entered the page 3,342 ms after the navigation began, in the base type, and took the display face when the file arrived. A failed load is handled by the loader: the links the import adds are noted as it starts, and when it fails each failed link is replaced at once by a fresh one whose address carries a query of its own (`?retry=1`), once; if that fails too the request settles as not loaded and the page is drawn in the type it had, a request made within 10 seconds of the failure (`RETRY_AFTER_MS`) takes the failure as it is, and a later one adds a fresh link again rather than calling `import()`, which would fetch nothing (see Verify items, "The retry after a failed load (step 30)"); an import that failed having added no link of its own (the development server, a unit test's stand-in) is called again by a later request.
- **The loading box.** While the page's code or the stylesheet is on its way the layout's boundary shows the site's loading line in a box at least the window's height (`min-h-screen`), so the footer stays below the window. A check in Chromium outside the suite, on the `a11y-on` build at 390 by 844 and 1280 by 800 pixels, measured what it does. Moving from `/` to `/about` inside the site (the address changed in place, with no reload), the layout shift after the move was 0.0000 at both widths, where the same layout with the site's plain loading line in the box moved the footer twice, 0.7011 in all at 1280 and 1.3436 at 390 (0.6109 and 1.4237 on `/governance/bylaws`, where the box leaves 0.0548 and 0.0801, the documents' lists arriving). On a first visit the site's own loading line in `src/App.tsx` stands while the layout's code arrives, and the first visit measured the same with either loading line in the box (`/about` 0.6718 at 390 and 0.3812 at 1280), so the page's own arrival is measured apart from the swap of the faces (see the browser runs and Deviations).
- **The hooks.** `src/contexts/heritage-layout.ts` holds `HeritageLayoutContext`, true inside the layout and false everywhere else, with three readers: `useInHeritageLayout`; `useHeritageHook`, which gives an element's `data-heritage` word inside the layout and nothing outside it, so React draws no attribute there; and `useHeritageOrnaments`, true inside the layout under `newLook` only. `PageHero` puts `display` on its h1, the one h1 of each of the six pages. The cards the pages draw as `rounded-xl border bg-card` take `card`: a visitor's seat cards on Board (an admin's seat cards and the Add a board seat card are forms, drawn in the base look with no hook), the join card on Annual meeting, the upcoming championship's card and the reigning champions' cards on Champions, and in `GovernanceDocuments` each document's card and the empty list's box; the Champions table's frame takes `table`. The About page's logo frame takes the 2px radius by its own slot (`data-slot="lca-logo-mat"`), cream on the paper with the heritage hairline. The section headings (20 pixels at most) take no display hook and keep the base face, since the display face is never under 32 pixels; no page shows a display figure, so `figure` is used nowhere and no copy is added for one; the reader hook is WS14's and `.small-caps` WS10's, and neither is used. Not hooked: the governance sidebar and tabs (the section's navigation), the navy call-to-action boxes, the dashed box Champions shows when it has no champions, which has no ground of its own, and the Agenda card on Annual meeting, which is commented out. Outside the layout every reader gets false, so `PageHero`'s nine other importers never take a hook, and with `themeHeritage` off the six pages draw today's markup to the attribute.
- **The ornaments.** `ThickThinRule` (`src/components/ThickThinRule.tsx`) is the board's rule drawn in CSS: a 6-pixel box with a 3-pixel line on top and a 1-pixel line below (`h-1.5 border-t-[3px] border-b`), the reverse with `edge="close"`, in the look's ink (`border-ink`), navy on the light grounds and light on the dark ones so it keeps showing in dark mode, or in brand gold on a navy band (`on="navy"`); it is decoration, hidden from screen readers. One opens each page under its heading band (in `GovLayout` for the four governance pages and in the page for the other two), and one parts each pair of a page's main sections: About's words from its call to join, Board's officers from its representatives and the board from its closing note, Bylaws' three lists of documents from each other and from the rules, Minutes' two lists, and Champions' upcoming championships, reigning champions and list of all champions; never one between items. `Seal` (`src/components/Seal.tsx`) is the seal of the decided Looks board on the Bylaws page: a navy disc (`fill-brand-navy`) inside two rings of brand gold (`stroke-lca-gold`, the gold only as the seal's line), with the rook drawn by `LcaMark` inside the seal's own SVG, so the path stays in `src/components/LcaMark.tsx`. `LcaMark` takes a size and no position, so the seal places it with its own geometry: the mark fills the seal's 100 by 100 box (`size-full`, a nested SVG's own size as well) and a group around it scales it to 34 units and moves it to the middle; that group gives it its white (`text-white`), and the mark carries no colour of its own. The board's seal has words round its rim, which are left out, so the seal adds no copy. It is hidden from screen readers and never focused, and nothing in either ornament moves or names a raw colour. `PageHero` draws the seal at 64 pixels on the right of the heading band from 640 pixels up (`hidden sm:block`), on a hero with no aside of its own, so each of the six pages has one.
- **GovernanceDocuments and the base reset.** `GovernanceDocuments` draws its add and edit card, which holds the title and date fields, the Write and Upload tabs and both calls of the lazy `RichTextEditor`, inside `ThemeScope scope="base"` when `themeHeritage` is on: the wrapper writes `data-theme=""`, which puts the base look back, and is `display: contents`, so it adds no box; with the switch off the card is drawn on its own, as it always was. The list of documents stays in the heritage look. A base scope with no scope around it is allowed, so nothing warns either way. The Board page does the same for an admin's forms: each seat card an admin edits (the seat's title, the holder's name where no member account is linked, and the photo) and the Add a board seat card are drawn whole in `ThemeScope scope="base"`, with no card hook, when `themeHeritage` is on, while a visitor's seat cards are not forms and keep the card hook; so every form on the six pages is in the base look. The editor is also imported, as before, by two admin screens that are always in the base look, `src/areas/admin/components/PostsPanel.tsx` and `src/pages/AdminEmailPage.tsx`.
- **The switches.** The layout waits for `themeHeritage`: `src/App.tsx` puts the routes inside it only when the switch is on, and `GovernanceDocuments` and the Board page add their base scopes only then; nothing else reads it, and `ThemeScope`, its loader and `src/lib/themeScopes.ts` name no switch. The look waits for `newLook` as well: its colours and its stylesheet's rules already did, and the rules and the seal, the one part of the layout a visitor would see with `newLook` off, are drawn only under it (`useHeritageOrnaments`), and the layout holds a page for the stylesheet only under it. So with `themeHeritage` on and `newLook` off the six pages are wrapped, carry their hooks and load the stylesheet without waiting for it, but look as they do today. The browser-test builds cannot show that case, since `a11y-on` turns both switches on and `a11y-off` neither; `test/a11y/global-setup.ts` and the tests that pin the two builds' switches are not changed, and the unit tests draw it with the switches mocked.
- **GovLayout's column.** Inside the layout `GovLayout`'s column is a div, so the four governance pages have one main, the site's; with `themeHeritage` off it stays the main it was, so their markup is today's and the four keep a main inside the site's main until WS14 rebuilds them (see Follow-ups).
- **The colour layer for AC13.** Measured first, with the same-run screenshots on `a11y-on` before the colour layer was changed: in the light look 20 of the 33 controls differed between the base and the heritage fixture, and in dark mode none, since heritage's dark tokens are the dark look's. The default Button's words were the paper (`rgb(247, 243, 232)` against `rgb(255, 255, 255)`), focused as well; the outline Button's ground, focused and under the pointer as well, and the field's ground, focused as well, were the paper against white; the secondary Button's ground, under the pointer as well, was the inset (`rgb(236, 228, 208)` against `rgb(247, 248, 250)`); the three filter chips and the three date blocks took the cream surface (`rgb(255, 253, 248)` against white) or the heritage hairline; the three status dots' words were heritage's muted (`rgb(94, 90, 82)` against `rgb(91, 100, 120)`); the muted pill took the inset and that muted; and the closed status tag took its inset hairline. The other 13, the link and gold Buttons and every status but the closed tag and the muted pill, were the same. The cause is the shadcn variables the controls read, which `src/index.css` points at the tokens heritage restyles (`--primary-foreground` at `--ground`, `--input` at `--field`, `--border` at `--hairline`, `--secondary`, `--muted` and `--accent` at `--surface-2`, `--muted-foreground` at `--ink-muted`), while the same variables paint the page's cards, lines and muted words. So `src/index.css` gains one rule after the heritage blocks: on the controls inside a heritage scope (the elements whose `data-slot` is `button`, `status-badge`, `status-dot`, `filter-chip` or `date-block`, the muted pill, found by its two classes `bg-muted` and `text-muted-foreground` since it has no slot, and `input`, `textarea` and `select`) the eight tokens heritage restyles in the light look take the base look's light values and the variables made from them are made again; in dark mode, on screens only, the same elements take those tokens from the element around them (`inherit`), since heritage's dark tokens are the dark look's already. The paper, the cards, the lines and the muted words around the controls stay heritage's, and the controls are the base look's: all 33 are the same byte for byte in light and dark. The tokens heritage changes in its own block (`test/unit/tokens-scopes.test.ts`), the contrast rows of `test/unit/contrast.test.ts` and the colours `test/a11y/scope-switch.spec.ts` expects, which it reads on the container and on the primary Button's ground, do not move; `test/unit/tokens.test.ts` holds the rule's dark half to screens only, as every dark rule is. The rule is 1,723 bytes of the production stylesheet as built.
- **ThemeScope.** `ThemeScope` keeps its props, its wrapper and its nesting check; its import of the looks' files moves to the loader, it exports `ScopeStylesheetReady` beside it, and its `as` prop no longer takes `main`, since a scope is never a page's main (see Follow-ups, "ThemeScope as a page's main (step 22)"): `test/unit/theme-scope.test.tsx` draws its box test as a section. Its header says where the loader is, what `ScopeStylesheetReady` holds and for how long.
- **The fixture page.** Only the heritage fixture changes: its h1 takes the display hook and its standings table the table hook, and after the base components it draws a card with the card hook and a base scope (`#fixture-base-in-heritage`), the one nesting the looks allow, holding a field and two Buttons, which the heritage spec reads. The base, live and scholastic fixtures draw what they drew; the switch tests read the base fixture, and the other specs count what the new parts add none of (the 13 statuses, the chips, the scroll panel's boxes and the tables' rows), so no count moves, and axe finds nothing on the heritage fixture with them.

The editor's library measures text through browser APIs jsdom lacks (`getClientRects` and `getBoundingClientRect` on a range, `elementFromPoint`), which the file gives stand-ins, in the file only. `test/unit/heritage-layout.test.tsx` holds each of the six pages, for a visitor and an admin, with `newLook` off and on, to the length and sha256 of its markup drawn from the files at `0cc7c30` (24 entries in `test/unit/fixtures/heritage-pages-today.ts`, drawn again from a copy of that commit for this record and found the same); inside the layout, each page in a div that is no main, with the look's ground and ink, its hooks, its rules and its seal under `newLook`, and none of either with `newLook` off; the page's markup inside the layout, with the hooks, the rules, the seal and the column taken back out, the markup it draws on its own; and the layout holding the page, its loading line in a box at least the window's height, until the stylesheet has arrived or failed. `test/unit/heritage-ornaments.test.tsx` holds the two ornaments to the board's shapes, their tokens, decoration and no colour on the mark; `test/unit/heritage-app-routes.test.tsx` draws `src/App.tsx` whole, header, main and footer, with the switch on and off, at the six addresses and the three old ones that lead to them; and `test/unit/heritage-controls-tokens.test.tsx` works out from `src/index.css`, as a browser cascades it, the colours of the controls inside heritage and base, light, dark and printed, and holds the rule for heritage's controls to the base look's values.

The run of the layout shift with a face of Georgia's metrics is K's, and K reviews the judgement calls and looks at the six pages on a phone and a wide screen, in the light look and dark mode (see Follow-ups).
- **Judgement calls.** K reviews these calls, with those of steps 23 to 30, before `newLook` and `themeHeritage` are turned on (see Follow-ups):
  - The hooks come from a context the layout provides, read by `PageHero`, `GovLayout`, `GovernanceDocuments` and the pages, rather than from `FEATURES.themeHeritage` in each file, so `PageHero`'s nine other importers never take a hook even with the switch on, and the six pages' markup with the switch off is today's.
  - The scope is a div inside the site's main rather than the main itself, as the spec's table words it, so a page keeps one main landmark.
  - `GovLayout`'s column is a div only inside the layout, so with the switch off its markup is today's; the four pages keep their second main until the switch is on or WS14 rebuilds them.
  - The paper ground runs down to the footer as a shadow of the box, rather than as a minimum height, which would push the footer of a short page below the window.
  - The thick-thin rules and the seal are drawn under `newLook` only, so with `themeHeritage` on and `newLook` off the pages look as they do today; the hooks, attributes the stylesheet reads only under `newLook`, are there either way.
  - The layout's loading box is at least the window's height. It keeps the footer below the window on a move inside the site (0.0000 against 0.70 at 1280 and 1.34 at 390 pixels on `/about` with the site's plain line) and changed nothing measured on a first visit, where the site's own line in `src/App.tsx` stands while the layout's code arrives; holding the height from the first paint would mean changing that line for every page loaded on demand.
  - AC11's 0.1 is held for the swap of the faces, measured from the start of the navigation apart from the page's own arrival, rather than for every shift from the start, which the page's arrival alone puts over 0.1 with every switch off.
  - Heritage's controls get the base tokens from one rule on the controls in `src/index.css`, rather than from the shadcn variables pointed back at base values in the heritage block: those variables also paint the page's card lines (`--border`), its muted words (`--muted-foreground`) and its panels (`--muted`), which stay heritage's. The muted pill is found by its two classes rather than by a slot added to StatusBadge's tone path, whose markup the tests hold to today's.
  - One thick-thin rule under each heading band and one between a page's main sections, never between items; one seal per page, in the heading band from 640 pixels up, where the band has room for it beside the title.
  - The seal is the board's navy disc and two gold rings with the rook, without the words round its rim, so it adds no copy.
  - The cards a page draws as `rounded-xl border bg-card` take the card hook; the governance sidebar and tabs, the navy call-to-action boxes and the dashed empty box on Champions keep their corners.
  - Every form on the six pages is in a base scope: on the Board page an admin's seat cards, which are forms for the seat, are reset whole, their frame with their fields, as the governance documents' add and edit card is, rather than only the fields inside a heritage card, so an admin sees the base look's cards where a visitor sees heritage's.
  - A failed stylesheet is tried once more at once, and again by a scope drawn 10 seconds or more after the failure, never by one drawn sooner, so a missing file is not asked for in a loop.
  - The layout holds a page for its stylesheet for three seconds at most (`HOLD_AT_MOST_MS`), and only under `newLook`: a file slower than that lets the page draw in the base type and move once when the file arrives, rather than keep a visitor from the page for a file of 2,836 bytes; with `newLook` off none of the file's rules apply, so nothing is held.
  - `ThemeScope`'s `as` no longer takes `main`.
  - The test with `themeHeritage` off holds each page's markup as its length and sha256, drawn from the files before they changed, rather than as literals, since the six pages' markup runs to 4,552 to 17,365 characters each.

### Step 32: AC1 in every look, and WS01 closed

The thirteenth and last step of checkpoint D, and of WS01. It adds `test/a11y/scopes.spec.ts`, the matrix of acceptance criterion 1: axe on every page the criterion names, in the light look, dark mode, the live look and heritage, at a desktop's and a phone's width, and on the scholastic fixture page, on the build with `newLook` and `themeHeritage` on. Its first run found three rules' findings on four pages, and each is fixed under `newLook` only: a rule in `src/index.css` underlines the State champions link; `src/pages/TournamentDetailPage.tsx` gives the pairings button white words and lets its one column shrink on a phone, the sections table scrolling in a named region; and `src/pages/ClubsPage.tsx` makes a club's name, not its card, the button that shows the club on the map, and lets a colour a club picked give way to the look's ink on a dark ground, through `clubTextOnDark` in `src/areas/clubs/clubColors.ts`, which a club's own page and the admin's colour preview take as well. A second rule in `src/index.css` draws the ring of a scrolling menu's options inside their edge, one of the follow-ups handed to this step. With `newLook` off every page draws what it drew, so `test/a11y/baseline.json` is unchanged. One change is made with every switch off, since it changes nothing seen: the buttons on the pages AC1 names that showed which of a set is picked by their look alone now say it to a screen reader, with `aria-pressed` (the bye rounds on the tournament page and in its family panel, and on `/tournaments` the Upcoming and Past tabs, the List and Calendar views, the calendar's days and the state filter's options) or `aria-current` (the event whose details are shown beside the list, and today's date in the calendar). `test/a11y/known-violations.json` keeps today's nine findings with every switch off and lists none for the build with the switches on. The records close WS01: every acceptance row ends with a passing test, a recorded measurement or an action of K's, and Checkpoint D, after this block, says what the merge does to production. No package is added, and nothing under `public/`, `functions/`, `workers/`, `domain/`, `migrations/` or `index.html` changes. The base was `c52848e` (step 31), with `453105b` after it, a commit between steps 31 and 32 that makes the two ring checks in `test/a11y/components-edges.spec.ts` poll until the ring is drawn, since the CI job on `c52848e` read the gold Button's ring on the build with no switch on before the ring had its width; nothing is committed yet.
